title.zh: 卷二百十七 列傳第一百〇五 王家屏 陳于陛 沈鯉 于慎行 李廷機 吳道南
title.en: Volume 217 Biographies 105: Wang Jiabing, Chen Yubi, Shen Li, Yu Shenxing, Li Tingji, Wu Daonan
title.raw: 卷二百十七 列傳第一百〇五 王家屏 陳于陛 沈鯉 于慎行 李廷機 吳道南 Volume 217 Biographies 105: Wang Jiabing, Chen Yubi, Shen Li, Yu Shenxing, Li Tingji, Wu Daonan

sentences.zh: 王家屏陳于陛沈鯉于慎行李廷機吳道南

translations.literal: Wang Jiabing, Chen Yubi, Shen Li, Yu Shenxing, Li Tingji, Wu Daonan
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jiabing, Chen Yubi, Shen Li, Yu Shenxing, Li Tingji, and Wu Daonan

sentences.zh: 王家屏

translations.literal: Wang Jiabing
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jiabing

sentences.zh: 王家屏，字忠伯，大同山陰人。

translations.literal: Wang Jiabing, style name Zhongbo, was a native of Shanyin in Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jiabing, whose style name was Zhongbo, came from Shanyin in Datong.

sentences.zh: 隆慶二年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the second year of Longqing.
translations.idiomatic: In 1568 he passed the metropolitan examination and received his jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 選庶吉士，授編修，預修《世宗實錄》。

translations.literal: He was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, appointed compiler, and took part in compiling the Veritable Records of Emperor Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: He was chosen for the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, made a compiler, and helped compile the Veritable Records of the Jiajing Emperor.

sentences.zh: 高拱兄捷前為操江都御史，以官帑遺趙文華，家屏直書之，時拱方柄國，囑稍諱，家屏執不可。

translations.literal: Gao Gong's elder brother Jie had previously been Censor-in-Chief of the Yangtze patrol; he had given official funds to Zhao Wenhua. Jiabing recorded this directly. At the time Gao Gong held power and asked him to soften it somewhat, but Jiabing firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gong's older brother Jie had once served as Censor-in-Chief on the Yangtze patrol and had diverted official funds to Zhao Wenhua. Wang Jiabing recorded this plainly in the Veritable Records. Gao Gong, who was then chief minister, urged him to soften the wording, but Wang Jiabing would not yield.

sentences.zh: 萬曆初，進修撰，充日講官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wanli he was promoted to senior compiler and served as a daily lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wanli reign he rose to senior compiler and was appointed a daily lecturer at court.

sentences.zh: 敷奏剴摯，帝嘗斂容受，稱為端士。

translations.literal: His presentations were earnest and sincere; the emperor would sit solemnly to receive them and called him an upright gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke before the throne with earnest clarity, and the emperor would listen with composed attention, praising him as a man of integrity.

sentences.zh: 張居正寢疾，詞臣率奔走禱祈，獨家屏不往。

translations.literal: When Zhang Juzheng lay ill, the literary officials all rushed to pray for him; Jiabing alone did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Juzheng fell gravely ill, his fellow literary officials hurried to offer prayers, but Wang Jiabing alone stayed away.

sentences.zh: 再遷侍講學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to be a lecturer-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to lecturer-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 十二年，擢禮部右侍郎，改吏部。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Rites and transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In 1584 he was made Right Vice Minister of Rites and then moved to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 甫逾月，命以左侍郎兼東閣大學士，入預機務。

translations.literal: Barely a month later, he was ordered to serve as Left Vice Minister while also holding the Eastern Pavilion Grand Secretaryship, entering to take part in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Only a month later he was named Left Vice Minister and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, and entered the inner circle of policy-making.

sentences.zh: 去史官二年即輔政，前此未有也。

translations.literal: Only two years after leaving the Historiography Office he was assisting in government—there had been nothing like it before.
translations.idiomatic: He reached the highest ministerial rank just two years after leaving the Historiography Office, a promotion without precedent.

sentences.zh: 申時行當國，許國、王錫爵次之，家屏居末。

translations.literal: Shen Shixing held the government; Xu Guo and Wang Xijue came next, and Jiabing ranked last.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Shixing headed the government, with Xu Guo and Wang Xijue after him; Wang Jiabing stood lowest in seniority among the grand secretaries.

sentences.zh: 每議事，秉正持法，不亢不隨。

translations.literal: Whenever matters were discussed, he upheld rectitude and held to the law, neither overbearing nor yielding.
translations.idiomatic: In council he held to principle and law, neither domineering nor pliant.

sentences.zh: 越二年，遭繼母憂。

translations.literal: After two years he was bereaved of his stepmother.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later his stepmother died, and he entered mourning.

sentences.zh: 詔賜銀幣，馳傳，行人護行。

translations.literal: An edict bestowed silver and silks, a fast courier relay, and an official to escort him on his journey.
translations.idiomatic: The throne granted him silver and silk, relay horses for his journey home, and an envoy to escort him.

sentences.zh: 服甫闋，詔進禮部尚書，遣行人召還。

translations.literal: When his mourning had barely ended, an edict promoted him to Minister of Rites and sent an envoy to summon him back.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as mourning ended he was promoted Minister of Rites and recalled to court by imperial messenger.

sentences.zh: 抵京師，三月未得見。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the capital, three months passed without his being received in audience.
translations.idiomatic: He reached the capital but could not obtain an audience for three months.

sentences.zh: 家屏以為言，請因聖節御殿受賀，畢發留中章奏，舉行冊立皇太子禮。

translations.literal: Jiabing spoke on this, asking that on the emperor's birthday he hold court to receive congratulations, then issue the memorials held in abeyance, and carry out the ceremony of investing the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jiabing remonstrated, urging that on the emperor's birthday he should hold court for congratulations, then release the backlog of memorials and perform the investiture of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No response was given.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave no reply.

sentences.zh: 復偕同官疏請。

translations.literal: Again he joined his colleagues in a memorial petition.
translations.idiomatic: He again joined his fellow ministers in a memorial petition.

sentences.zh: 帝乃於萬壽節強一臨御焉。

translations.literal: The emperor then forced himself to appear at court once on his birthday.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor finally forced himself to hold court once on his birthday.

sentences.zh: 俄遣中官諭家屏，獎以忠愛。

translations.literal: Soon a eunuch was sent to instruct Jiabing, praising his loyalty and devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the emperor sent a eunuch to praise Wang Jiabing for his loyal devotion.

sentences.zh: 家屏疏謝，復請帝勤視朝。

translations.literal: Jiabing memorialized thanks and again asked the emperor to attend court diligently.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jiabing memorialized his thanks and again urged the emperor to attend court regularly.

sentences.zh: 居數日，帝為一御門延見，自是益深居不出矣。

translations.literal: After several days the emperor once held court at the Gate to receive audiences; thereafter he withdrew ever deeper and never came out.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later the emperor held court once at the Gate, but thereafter withdrew ever deeper into the palace and rarely appeared again.

sentences.zh: 評事雒于仁進四箴，帝將重罪之。

translations.literal: The case reviewer Luo Yuren submitted four admonitions; the emperor was about to punish him severely.
translations.idiomatic: The case reviewer Luo Yuren submitted four admonitions to the throne, and the emperor was about to punish him severely.

sentences.zh: 家屏言：「人主出入起居之節，耳目心誌之娛，庶官不及知、不敢諫者，輔弼之臣得先知而預諫之，故能防欲於微渺。

translations.literal: Jiabing said: 'The sovereign's comings and goings, his daily routine, and the pleasures of eye, ear, mind, and will are matters that ordinary officials cannot know of or dare to remonstrate about. Assisting ministers, learning of them first, can remonstrate in advance and thus check desire while it is still slight.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jiabing said: 'A ruler's comings and goings, his daily routine, and the pleasures that fill eye, ear, mind, and will are things ordinary officials neither know of nor dare to criticize. Assisting ministers who learn of them first can remonstrate in advance and thus curb desire while it is still slight.

sentences.zh: 今于仁以庶僚上言，而臣備位密勿，反緘默茍容，上虧聖明之譽，下陷庶僚蒙不測之威，臣罪大矣，尚可一日立於聖世哉！」

translations.literal: Now Yuren, a junior official, has spoken up, while I, holding a confidential post close to the throne, have instead kept silent and tolerated wrongdoing, diminishing Your Majesty's reputation for sagacity above and exposing junior officials below to unforeseen severity. My offense is grave—how can I still stand one day in this enlightened age!
translations.idiomatic: Now Yuren, a junior official, has spoken up, while I, holding a confidential post at your side, have kept silent and tolerated wrongdoing instead—diminishing Your Majesty's reputation for sagacity above and exposing junior officials below to unforeseen punishment. My offense is grave. How can I still stand one day in this enlightened age?

sentences.zh: 帝不懌，留中，而于仁得善去。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and kept the memorial in abeyance, but Yuren was able to leave without punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased and kept the memorial in abeyance, but Luo Yuren was able to withdraw without punishment.

sentences.zh: 十八年，以久旱乞罷，言：「邇年以來，天鳴地震，星隕風霾，川竭河涸，加以旱潦蝗螟，疫癘劄瘥，調燮之難，莫甚今日。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, citing prolonged drought, he asked to resign, saying: 'In recent years heaven has thundered, the earth has quaked, stars have fallen, winds and mists have risen, rivers have dried and streams have failed; to this have been added drought and flood, locusts and caterpillars, pestilence and plague. The difficulty of harmonizing heaven and earth has never been greater than today.
translations.idiomatic: In 1590, citing prolonged drought, he asked to resign, saying: 'In recent years heaven has thundered, the earth has quaked, stars have fallen, and winds and mists have darkened the sky; rivers have dried and streams have failed. To this have been added drought and flood, locusts and caterpillars, pestilence and plague. The task of harmonizing heaven and earth has never been harder than it is today.

sentences.zh: 況套賊跳梁於陜右，土蠻猖獗於遼西，貢市屬國復鴟張虎視於宣、大。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Tatars are rampant in western Shaanxi, the Tümed are fierce in western Liaodong, and tributary states at the markets are again spreading their wings and glaring like tigers at Xuanfu and Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Tatars are on the march in western Shaanxi, the Tümed are fierce in western Liaodong, and tributary peoples at the border markets are again spreading their wings and glaring like tigers toward Xuanfu and Datong.

sentences.zh: 虛內事外，內已竭而外患未休；

translations.literal: The interior is drained to serve the frontier; within, resources are exhausted, yet external troubles do not cease;
translations.idiomatic: The interior is drained to serve the frontier: within, resources are exhausted, yet external troubles do not cease;

sentences.zh: 剝民供軍，民已窮而軍食未裕。

translations.literal: the people are stripped to supply the army; the people are already destitute while military provisions are still insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: the people are stripped to supply the army—the people are already destitute while military provisions are still insufficient.

sentences.zh: 且議論紛紜，罕持大體；

translations.literal: Moreover, debate is confused and few hold to the larger principles;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, debate is confused and few hold to the larger principles;

sentences.zh: 簿書淩雜，只飾靡文。

translations.literal: documents pile up in disorder, serving only to adorn empty rhetoric.
translations.idiomatic: documents pile up in disorder, serving only to adorn empty rhetoric.

sentences.zh: 綱維縱弛，愒玩之習成；

translations.literal: The bonds of governance are slack, and habits of indolence have formed;
translations.idiomatic: The bonds of governance are slack, and habits of indolence have taken hold;

sentences.zh: 名實混淆，僥幸之風啟。

translations.literal: name and reality are confused, and a wind of opportunism has risen.
translations.idiomatic: name and reality are confused, and a wind of opportunism has risen.

sentences.zh: 陛下又深居靜攝，朝講希臨。

translations.literal: Your Majesty moreover dwells deep in seclusion and quiet restraint, rarely attending court lectures.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty moreover dwells deep in seclusion, rarely attending court lectures or audiences.

sentences.zh: 統計臣一歲間，僅兩覲天顏而已。

translations.literal: Counting up, in one year your servant has seen the imperial countenance only twice.
translations.idiomatic: Counting up, in one year I have seen Your Majesty's face only twice.

sentences.zh: 間嘗一進瞽言，竟與諸司章奏並寢不行。

translations.literal: Once I ventured a blind man's word, yet it was shelved along with the memorials of all the offices and not acted upon.
translations.idiomatic: Once I ventured a frank word, yet it was shelved along with the memorials of all the offices and never acted upon.

sentences.zh: 今驕陽爍石，小民愁苦之聲殷天震地，而獨未徹九閽。

translations.literal: Now the fierce sun scorches stone; the cries of the common people's distress fill heaven and shake the earth, yet they have not reached the nine gates.
translations.idiomatic: Now the fierce sun scorches the stones; the cries of the common people's distress fill heaven and shake the earth, yet they have not reached Your Majesty's ears.

sentences.zh: 此臣所以中夜旁皇，飲食俱廢，不能自已者也。

translations.literal: This is why your servant wanders in distress at midnight, food and drink abandoned, unable to restrain himself.
translations.idiomatic: This is why I wander in distress at midnight, unable to eat or sleep, unable to restrain myself.

sentences.zh: 乞賜罷歸，用避賢路。」

translations.literal: I beg to be dismissed and sent home, to clear the way for the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: I beg to be dismissed and sent home, to clear the way for the worthy.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No response was given.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave no reply.

sentences.zh: 時儲位未定，廷臣交章請冊立。

translations.literal: At the time the heir apparent had not been fixed, and court officials submitted memorial after memorial requesting investiture.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the heir apparent had not been designated, and court officials submitted memorial after memorial requesting investiture.

sentences.zh: 其年十月，閣臣合疏以去就爭。

translations.literal: That year in the tenth month the grand secretaries submitted a joint memorial, pressing the issue with threats of resignation.
translations.idiomatic: That October the grand secretaries submitted a joint memorial, pressing the issue with threats of resignation.

sentences.zh: 帝不悅，傳諭數百言，切責廷臣沽名激擾，指為悖逆。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and issued an oral instruction of several hundred words, sharply rebuking the court officials for fishing for fame and stirring up trouble, calling them rebellious.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased and issued an oral instruction of several hundred words, sharply rebuking the court officials for fishing for fame and stirring up trouble, calling them rebellious.

sentences.zh: 時行等相顧錯愕，各具疏再爭，杜門乞去。

translations.literal: Shixing and the others looked at one another in dismay, each submitted a memorial to argue again, and shut their doors, begging to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Shixing and the others looked at one another in dismay, each submitted another memorial to argue the point, and shut their doors, begging to resign.

sentences.zh: 獨家屏在閣，復請速決大計。

translations.literal: Jiabing alone remained in the Secretariat and again asked that the great decision be settled quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jiabing alone remained in the Secretariat and again urged a swift decision on the great matter.

sentences.zh: 帝乃遣內侍傳語，期以明年春夏，廷臣無所奏擾，即於冬間議行，否則待逾十五歲。

translations.literal: The emperor then sent a eunuch with a message, setting the next spring or summer as the date; if the court officials made no further memorials to disturb him, it would be carried out in winter; otherwise he would wait until the prince was over fifteen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sent a eunuch with a message, setting the following spring or summer as the date; if the court officials made no further memorials to disturb him, the investiture would be carried out in winter; otherwise he would wait until the prince was over fifteen.

sentences.zh: 家屏以口敕難據，欲帝特頒詔諭，立具草進。

translations.literal: Jiabing held that an oral command was hard to rely on and wanted the emperor to issue a special edict; he immediately drafted one and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jiabing held that an oral command was hard to rely on and wanted the emperor to issue a special edict; he immediately drafted one and submitted it.

sentences.zh: 帝不用，復諭二十年春舉行。

translations.literal: The emperor did not use it and again instructed that it would be carried out in the spring of the twentieth year.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not use it and again instructed that the investiture would be carried out in the spring of 1592.

sentences.zh: 家屏喜，即宣示外廷，外廷歡然。

translations.literal: Jiabing was pleased and at once announced it to the outer court; the outer court rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jiabing was pleased and at once announced it to the outer court, which rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 而帝意實猶豫，聞家屏宣示，弗善也，傳諭詰責。

translations.literal: But the emperor's mind was in fact still hesitant; hearing that Jiabing had announced it, he was displeased and sent an oral instruction to rebuke him.
translations.idiomatic: But the emperor's mind was still hesitant; hearing that Wang Jiabing had announced it, he was displeased and sent an oral instruction to rebuke him.

sentences.zh: 時行等合詞謝，乃已。

translations.literal: Shixing and the others submitted a joint apology, and the matter ended.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Shixing and the others submitted a joint apology, and the matter ended.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，工部主事張有德以冊立儀註請。

translations.literal: The next autumn Zhang Youde, a principal clerk in the Ministry of Works, requested the ceremonial regulations for investiture.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn Zhang Youde, a principal clerk in the Ministry of Works, requested the ceremonial regulations for investiture.

sentences.zh: 帝復以為激擾，命止其事。

translations.literal: The emperor again regarded it as provocative disturbance and ordered the matter stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again regarded it as provocative disturbance and ordered the matter stopped.

sentences.zh: 國執爭去，時行被人言，不得已亦去，錫爵先以省親歸，家屏遂為首輔。

translations.literal: Xu Guo pressed his argument and left; Shixing, attacked by rumor, also left as he had no choice; Xijue had already returned home to visit his parents; Jiabing thus became chief grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guo pressed his argument and resigned; Shen Shixing, attacked by rumor, also resigned as he had no choice; Wang Xijue had already returned home to visit his parents; Wang Jiabing thus became chief grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 以國諫疏己列名，不當獨留，再疏乞罷。

translations.literal: Because his name had been on Guo's remonstrance memorial, he ought not to remain alone; he submitted another memorial begging to resign.
translations.idiomatic: Because his name had been on Xu Guo's remonstrance memorial, he felt he ought not to remain alone and submitted another memorial begging to resign.

sentences.zh: 不允，乃視事。

translations.literal: This was not granted, and he then took up his duties.
translations.idiomatic: This was not granted, and he then took up his duties.

sentences.zh: 家屏制行端嚴，推誠秉公，百司事一無所撓。

translations.literal: Jiabing's conduct was upright and strict; he extended sincerity and held to fairness, and in the affairs of the hundred offices he yielded to none.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jiabing's conduct was upright and strict; he acted with sincerity and fairness, and in the affairs of the hundred offices he yielded to no pressure.

sentences.zh: 性忠讜，好直諫。

translations.literal: By nature he was loyal and outspoken and loved to remonstrate directly.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was loyal and outspoken and loved to remonstrate directly.

sentences.zh: 冊立期數更，中外議論紛然。

translations.literal: The date of investiture was changed several times, and debate within and without the court was confused.
translations.idiomatic: The date of investiture was changed several times, and debate within and without the court grew confused.

sentences.zh: 家屏深憂之，力請踐大信，以塞口語，消宮闈釁。

translations.literal: Jiabing was deeply troubled and pressed strongly to fulfill the great pledge, to stop loose talk and dispel strife within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jiabing was deeply troubled and pressed strongly to fulfill the great pledge, to stop loose talk and dispel strife within the palace.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No response was given.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave no reply.

sentences.zh: 二十年春，給事中李獻可等請豫教，帝黜之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twentieth year the supervising secretary Li Xiankuo and others asked for early instruction of the heir; the emperor dismissed them.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1592 the supervising secretary Li Xiankuo and others asked for early instruction of the heir apparent; the emperor dismissed them.

sentences.zh: 家屏封還御批力諫。

translations.literal: Jiabing returned the imperial rescript sealed and remonstrated forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jiabing returned the imperial rescript sealed and remonstrated forcefully.

sentences.zh: 帝益怒，譴謫者相屬。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angrier still, and those rebuked and banished followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angrier still, and rebukes and banishments followed one after another.

sentences.zh: 家屏遂引疾求罷，上言：「漢汲黯有言：『天子置公卿輔弼之臣，寧令從臾承意陷主於不義乎！』

translations.literal: Jiabing then cited illness and asked to resign, stating: 'The Han official Ji An once said: "The Son of Heaven appoints dukes and ministers as assisting and supporting officials—would he have them follow his whims and carry out his wishes, leading the ruler into unrighteousness!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jiabing then cited illness and asked to resign, stating: 'The Han official Ji An once said: "The Son of Heaven appoints dukes and ministers as assisting officials—would he have them follow his whims and carry out his wishes, leading the ruler into unrighteousness!

sentences.zh: 每感斯言，惕然內愧。

translations.literal: Whenever I am moved by these words, I am inwardly ashamed and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I reflect on these words, I am inwardly ashamed and fearful.

sentences.zh: 頃年以來，九閽重閉，宴安懷毒，郊廟不饗，堂陛不交。

translations.literal: In recent years the nine gates have been heavily shut; ease and comfort harbor poison; suburban and ancestral temples go without offerings; hall and steps do not meet.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the nine gates have been heavily shut; ease and comfort harbor poison; suburban and ancestral temples go without offerings; ruler and ministers do not meet.

sentences.zh: 天災物怪，罔徹宸聰；

translations.literal: Heavenly disasters and strange portents do not reach the imperial hearing;
translations.idiomatic: Heavenly disasters and strange portents do not reach Your Majesty's ears;

sentences.zh: 國計民生，莫關聖慮。

translations.literal: state policy and the people's livelihood do not touch the imperial concern.
translations.idiomatic: state policy and the people's livelihood do not touch Your Majesty's concern.

sentences.zh: 臣備員輔弼，曠職鰥官，久當退避。

translations.literal: Your servant fills a post among the assistants, neglecting his duties like a widowed official; long ago he ought to have withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: I fill a post among your assistants, neglecting my duties like a widowed official; long ago I ought to have withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 今數月間，請朝講，請廟饗，請元旦受賀，請大計臨朝，悉寢不報。

translations.literal: In recent months I have asked for court lectures, for temple offerings, for New Year's Day congratulations, for attendance at the grand review—all have been shelved without response.
translations.idiomatic: In recent months I have asked for court lectures, for temple offerings, for New Year's Day congratulations, for attendance at the grand review—all have been shelved without response.

sentences.zh: 臣犬馬微誠，不克感回天意，已可見矣。

translations.literal: Your servant's slight loyalty like a dog or horse cannot move heaven's will back—it is already plain to see.
translations.idiomatic: My slight loyalty cannot move heaven's will back—it is already plain to see.

sentences.zh: 至豫教皇儲，自宣早計，奈何厭聞直言，概加貶謫。

translations.literal: As for early instruction of the imperial heir, it is plainly a matter to plan early—why dislike to hear straight words and punish all with banishment?
translations.idiomatic: As for early instruction of the imperial heir, it is plainly a matter to plan early—why dislike straight words and punish all with banishment?

sentences.zh: 臣誠不忍明主蒙弗諫之名，熙朝有橫施之罰，故冒死屢陳。

translations.literal: Your servant truly cannot bear that an enlightened ruler should bear the name of one who will not be remonstrated with, or that a glorious age should have punishments meted out arbitrarily; therefore he has risked death to speak repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: I truly cannot bear that an enlightened ruler should bear the name of one who will not be remonstrated with, or that a glorious age should have punishments meted out arbitrarily; therefore I have risked death to speak repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 若依違保祿，淟涊茍容，汲黯所謂『陷主不義』者，臣死不敢出此，願賜骸骨還田里。」

translations.literal: If I were to waver and preserve my salary, to be base and tolerate wrongdoing—the thing Ji An called 'leading the ruler into unrighteousness'—your servant would not dare do this even on pain of death. I beg to be granted my bones and sent back to my fields.'
translations.idiomatic: If I were to waver and preserve my salary, to be base and tolerate wrongdoing—the thing Ji An called 'leading the ruler into unrighteousness'—I would not dare do this even on pain of death. I beg to be granted my bones and sent back to my fields.'

sentences.zh: 帝得奏不下。

translations.literal: The emperor received the memorial but did not issue it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received the memorial but kept it in abeyance.

sentences.zh: 次輔趙志臯亦為家屏具揭。

translations.literal: The second grand secretary Zhao Zhigao also submitted a report on Jiabing's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: The second grand secretary Zhao Zhigao also submitted a report on Wang Jiabing's behalf.

sentences.zh: 帝遂責家屏希名托疾。

translations.literal: The emperor then rebuked Jiabing for fishing for fame and feigning illness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then rebuked Wang Jiabing for fishing for fame and feigning illness.

sentences.zh: 家屏復奏，言：「名非臣所敢棄，顧臣所希者，陛下為堯、舜之主，臣為堯、舜之臣，則名垂千載，沒有餘榮。

translations.literal: Jiabing memorialized again, saying: 'Fame is not something your servant dares to cast aside; what your servant hopes for is that Your Majesty be a ruler like Yao and Shun and your servant be a minister like Yao and Shun's—then fame would last a thousand years and there would be glory after death.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jiabing memorialized again, saying: 'Fame is not something I dare cast aside; what I hope for is that Your Majesty be a ruler like Yao and Shun and I be a minister like theirs—then fame would last a thousand years and there would be glory after death.

sentences.zh: 若徒犯顏觸忌，抗爭僨事，被譴罷歸，何名之有！

translations.literal: If one merely offends the countenance and touches taboos, struggles in vain and is rebuked and sent home, what fame is there!
translations.idiomatic: If one merely offends the countenance and touches taboos, struggles in vain and is rebuked and sent home, what fame is there!

sentences.zh: 必不希名，將使臣身處高官，家享厚祿，主愆莫正，政亂莫匡，可謂不希名之臣矣，國家奚賴焉？

translations.literal: If one must not seek fame, your servant would hold high office and his family enjoy rich salary while the ruler's faults go uncorrected and disorder goes unreformed—such a one could be called a minister who does not seek fame; on what could the state rely?
translations.idiomatic: If one must not seek fame, I would hold high office and my family enjoy rich salary while the ruler's faults go uncorrected and disorder goes unreformed—such a one could be called a minister who does not seek fame; on what could the state rely?

sentences.zh: 更使臣棄名不顧，逢迎為悅，阿諛取容，許敬宗、李林甫之奸佞，無不可為，九廟神靈必陰殛臣，豈特得罪於李獻可諸臣已哉！」

translations.literal: To make your servant cast aside fame and not care, to please by flattery, to fawn and win favor—the treacherous wickedness of Xu Jingzong and Li Linfu would be nothing I could not do; the spirits of the nine temples would surely secretly strike me down—how much more than merely offending Li Xiankuo and the others!'
translations.idiomatic: To make me cast aside fame and not care, to please by flattery, to fawn and win favor—the treacherous wickedness of Xu Jingzong and Li Linfu would be nothing I could not do; the spirits of the nine temples would surely secretly strike me down—how much more than merely offending Li Xiankuo and the others!'

sentences.zh: 疏入，帝益不悅。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor was still more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial entered, the emperor was still more displeased.

sentences.zh: 遣內侍至邸，責以徑駁御批，故激主怒，且托疾要君。

translations.literal: He sent a eunuch to Jiabing's residence, rebuking him for directly rejecting the imperial rescript, deliberately stirring the ruler's anger, and feigning illness to coerce the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a eunuch to Wang Jiabing's residence, rebuking him for directly rejecting the imperial rescript, deliberately stirring the ruler's anger, and feigning illness to coerce the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 家屏言：「言涉至親，不宜有怒。

translations.literal: Jiabing said: 'When words concern one's closest kin, anger is not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jiabing said: 'When words concern one's closest kin, anger is not fitting.

sentences.zh: 事關典禮，不宜有怒。

translations.literal: When the matter concerns ritual and ceremony, anger is not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter concerns ritual and ceremony, anger is not fitting.

sentences.zh: 臣與諸臣但知為宗社大計，盡言效忠而已，豈意激皇上之怒哉？」

translations.literal: Your servant and the other officials know only to speak for the great plan of altar and state, to offer loyal words—that is all; how could we have meant to stir Your Majesty's anger?
translations.idiomatic: I and the other officials know only to speak for the great plan of altar and state, to offer loyal words—that is all; how could we have meant to stir Your Majesty's anger?

sentences.zh: 於是求去益力。

translations.literal: Thereupon he pressed his request to leave all the more strongly.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he pressed his request to resign all the more strongly.

sentences.zh: 或勸少需就大事。

translations.literal: Some urged him to wait a little and see the great matter through.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to wait a little and see the great matter through.

sentences.zh: 家屏曰：「人君惟所欲為者，由大臣持祿，小臣畏罪，有輕群下心。

translations.literal: Jiabing said: 'What a ruler wishes to do he can do because great ministers hold their salaries and junior officials fear punishment—there is contempt for the hearts of the multitude below.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jiabing said: 'What a ruler wishes to do he can do because great ministers hold their salaries and junior officials fear punishment—there is contempt for the hearts of the multitude below.

sentences.zh: 吾意大臣不愛爵祿，小臣不畏刑誅，事庶有濟耳。」

translations.literal: In my view, if great ministers do not love rank and salary and junior officials do not fear punishment by law, matters may yet be helped.
translations.idiomatic: In my view, if great ministers do not love rank and salary and junior officials do not fear punishment by law, matters may yet be helped.

sentences.zh: 遂復兩疏懇請。

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted two more memorials earnestly requesting leave.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he submitted two more memorials earnestly requesting leave.

sentences.zh: 詔馳傳歸。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him home by fast relay.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him home by fast relay.

sentences.zh: 家屏柄國止半載，又強半杜門，以戇直去國，朝野惜焉。

translations.literal: Jiabing held power for only half a year, and for more than half of that he shut his doors; he left the state for his blunt integrity, and court and countryside alike regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jiabing held power for only half a year, and for more than half of that he shut his doors; he left office for his blunt integrity, and court and countryside alike regretted it.

sentences.zh: 越八年，儲位始定。

translations.literal: Eight years later the heir was at last fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Eight years later the heir apparent was at last designated.

sentences.zh: 遣官賫敕存問，賚金幣羊酒。

translations.literal: Officials were sent bearing an imperial edict to inquire after his health, bestowing gold, silks, sheep, and wine.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were sent bearing an imperial edict to inquire after his health, bestowing gold, silks, sheep, and wine.

sentences.zh: 又二年卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: Two years later he died, aged sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he died, aged sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈少保，謚文端。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Junior Mentor and given the posthumous title Wenuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Junior Mentor and given the posthumous title Wenuan.

sentences.zh: 熹宗立，再贈太保，任一子尚寶丞。

translations.literal: When the Xizong emperor ascended, he was further posthumously made Grand Mentor, and one son was appointed Director of the Imperial Treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xizong emperor ascended, he was further posthumously made Grand Mentor, and one son was appointed Director of the Imperial Treasuries.

sentences.zh: 家屏家居時，朝鮮用兵。

translations.literal: While Jiabing lived at home, war broke out in Korea.
translations.idiomatic: While Wang Jiabing lived in retirement, war broke out in Korea.

sentences.zh: 貽書經略顧養謙曰：「昔衛為狄滅，齊桓率諸侯城楚丘，《春秋》高其義；

translations.literal: He wrote to the frontier commissioner Gu Yangqian: 'In antiquity when Wei was destroyed by the Di, Duke Huan of Qi led the feudal lords to wall Qiu; the Spring and Autumn Annals praise his righteousness;
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to the frontier commissioner Gu Yangqian: 'In antiquity when Wei was destroyed by the Di, Duke Huan of Qi led the feudal lords to wall Qiu; the Spring and Autumn Annals praise his righteousness;

sentences.zh: 未聞遂與狄仇，連諸侯兵以伐之也。

translations.literal: we never hear that he then made enemies of the Di and led the allied states' armies to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: we never hear that he then made enemies of the Di and led the allied states' armies to attack them.

sentences.zh: 今第以保會稽之恥，激厲朝鮮，以城楚丘之功，獎率將吏，無為主而為客，則善矣。」

translations.literal: Now you need only take the shame of Kuaiji as a spur, encourage Korea, and reward officers and men with the merit of walling Qiu—do not act as host while acting as guest, and all will be well.
translations.idiomatic: Now you need only take the shame of Kuaiji as a spur, encourage Korea, and reward officers and men with the merit of walling Qiu—do not act as host while acting as guest, and all will be well.

sentences.zh: 養謙不能用，朝鮮兵數年無功。

translations.literal: Yangqian could not adopt this counsel, and the Korean campaign went without success for years.
translations.idiomatic: Yangqian could not adopt this counsel, and the Korean campaign went without success for years.

sentences.zh: 其深識有謀，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His far-sighted counsel and stratagem were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His far-sighted counsel and stratagem were all of this kind.

sentences.zh: 陳于陛

translations.literal: Chen Yubi
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yubi

sentences.zh: 陳于陛，字元忠，大學士以勤子也。

translations.literal: Chen Yubi, style name Yuanzhong, was the son of Grand Secretary Chen Yiqin.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yubi, whose style name was Yuanzhong, was the son of Grand Secretary Chen Yiqin.

sentences.zh: 隆慶二年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the second year of Longqing.
translations.idiomatic: In 1568 he passed the metropolitan examination and received his jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: He was selected as a Hanlin bachelor and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was chosen for the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor and made a compiler.

sentences.zh: 萬曆初，預修世、穆兩朝實錄，充日講官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wanli he took part in compiling the Veritable Records of the Shizong and Muzong reigns and served as a daily lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wanli reign he helped compile the Veritable Records of the Jiajing and Longqing reigns and served as a daily lecturer at court.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍講學士，擢詹事，掌翰林院。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to lecturer-in-waiting, promoted to Grand Mentor, and put in charge of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to lecturer-in-waiting, was promoted Grand Mentor, and put in charge of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 疏請早建東宮。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking that the Eastern Palace be established early.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized asking that the heir apparent be designated early.

sentences.zh: 十九年，拜禮部右侍郎，領詹事府事。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was appointed Right Vice Minister of Rites and put in charge of the Grand Mentor's office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1591 he was appointed Right Vice Minister of Rites and put in charge of the Grand Mentor's office.

sentences.zh: 明年，改吏部，進左侍郎，教習庶吉士。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, promoted to Left Vice Minister, and instructed the Hanlin bachelors.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, promoted to Left Vice Minister, and instructed the Hanlin bachelors.

sentences.zh: 奏言元子不當封王，請及時冊立豫教，又請早朝勤政，皆不報。

translations.literal: He memorialized that the eldest son ought not to be enfeoffed as a prince, asked for timely investiture and early instruction, and again asked for early court attendance and diligent government—all without response.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that the eldest son ought not to be enfeoffed as a prince, asked for timely investiture and early instruction, and again asked for early court attendance and diligent government—all without response.

sentences.zh: 又明年，進禮部尚書，仍領詹事府事。

translations.literal: The year after that he was promoted to Minister of Rites while still heading the Grand Mentor's office.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that he was promoted Minister of Rites while still heading the Grand Mentor's office.

sentences.zh: 于陛少從父以勤習國家故實。

translations.literal: From youth Yubi studied with his father Yiqin the established facts of the state.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Chen Yubi studied with his father Yiqin the established facts of the state.

sentences.zh: 為史官，益究經世學。

translations.literal: As a historiographer he pursued statecraft all the more deeply.
translations.idiomatic: As a historiographer he pursued statecraft all the more deeply.

sentences.zh: 以前代皆修國史，疏言：「臣考史家之法，紀、表、誌、傳謂之正史。

translations.literal: Because previous dynasties all compiled national histories, he memorialized: 'Your servant has examined historians' methods: annals, tables, treatises, and biographies are called the standard history.
translations.idiomatic: Because previous dynasties all compiled national histories, he memorialized: 'I have examined historians' methods: annals, tables, treatises, and biographies are called the standard history.

sentences.zh: 宋去我朝近，制尤可考。

translations.literal: The Song is close to our dynasty, and its institutions are especially worth consulting.
translations.idiomatic: The Song is close to our dynasty, and its institutions are especially worth consulting.

sentences.zh: 真宗祥符間，王旦等撰進太祖、太宗兩朝正史。

translations.literal: In the Xiangfu era of Emperor Zhenzong, Wang Dan and others compiled and presented the standard histories of the Taizu and Taizong reigns.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiangfu era of Emperor Zhenzong, Wang Dan and others compiled and presented the standard histories of the Taizu and Taizong reigns.

sentences.zh: 仁宗天聖間，呂夷簡等增入真宗朝，名《三朝國史》。

translations.literal: In the Tiansheng era of Emperor Renzong, Lü Yijian and others added the Zhenzong reign, naming it the National History of Three Reigns.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tiansheng era of Emperor Renzong, Lü Yijian and others added the Zhenzong reign, naming it the National History of Three Reigns.

sentences.zh: 此則本朝君臣自修本朝正史之明證也。

translations.literal: This is clear proof that rulers and ministers of a dynasty compile their own dynasty's standard history.
translations.idiomatic: This is clear proof that rulers and ministers of a dynasty compile their own dynasty's standard history.

sentences.zh: 我朝史籍，止有列聖實錄，正史闕焉未講。

translations.literal: Our dynasty's historical records consist only of the successive emperors' Veritable Records; the standard history has not yet been undertaken.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty's historical records consist only of the successive emperors' Veritable Records; the standard history has not yet been undertaken.

sentences.zh: 伏睹朝野所撰次，可備采擇者無慮數百種。

translations.literal: I observe that works compiled at court and in the countryside suitable for selection number no fewer than several hundred kinds.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that works compiled at court and in the countryside suitable for selection number no fewer than several hundred kinds.

sentences.zh: 倘不及時網羅，歲月浸邈，卷帙散脫，耆舊漸雕，事跡罕據。

translations.literal: If we do not gather them in time, as years lengthen scrolls will scatter and fall away, the old will gradually pass, and deeds will rarely be attested.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not gather them in time, as years lengthen scrolls will scatter and fall away, the old will gradually pass, and deeds will rarely be attested.

sentences.zh: 欲成信史，將不可得。

translations.literal: To complete a trustworthy history will then be impossible.
translations.idiomatic: To complete a trustworthy history will then be impossible.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下立下明詔，設局編輯，使一代經制典章，犁然可考，鴻謨偉烈，光炳天壤，豈非萬世不朽盛事哉！」

translations.literal: May Your Majesty issue a clear edict and establish a bureau to compile and edit, so that the institutions and regulations of an age may be clearly consultable and great plans and splendid achievements may shine throughout heaven and earth—is this not an imperishable undertaking for ten thousand generations!
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty issue a clear edict and establish a bureau to compile and edit, so that the institutions and regulations of an age may be clearly consultable and great plans and splendid achievements may shine throughout heaven and earth—is this not an imperishable undertaking for ten thousand generations!

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved this.

sentences.zh: 二十二年三月，遂命詞臣分曹類纂，以于陛及尚書沈一貫、少詹事馮琦為副總裁，而閣臣總裁之。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twenty-second year the literary officials were ordered to compile by sections; Yubi, Minister Shen Yiguan, and Junior Grand Mentor Feng Qi were made deputy chief compilers, with the grand secretaries as chief compilers.
translations.idiomatic: In March 1594 the literary officials were ordered to compile by sections; Chen Yubi, Minister Shen Yiguan, and Junior Grand Mentor Feng Qi were made deputy chief compilers, with the grand secretaries as chief compilers.

sentences.zh: 其年夏，首輔王錫爵謝政，遂命于陛兼東閣大學士，入參機務。

translations.literal: That summer the chief grand secretary Wang Xijue resigned from government, and Yubi was ordered to hold concurrently the Eastern Pavilion Grand Secretaryship and enter to take part in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That summer the chief grand secretary Wang Xijue resigned from government, and Chen Yubi was ordered to hold concurrently the Eastern Pavilion Grand Secretaryship and enter to take part in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 疏陳親大臣、錄遺賢、獎外吏、核邊餉、儲將才、擇邊吏六事。

translations.literal: He memorialized setting forth six matters: drawing close to great ministers, recording overlooked worthies, rewarding frontier officials, auditing frontier supplies, storing up general talent, and selecting frontier officials.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized setting forth six matters: drawing close to great ministers, recording overlooked worthies, rewarding frontier officials, auditing frontier supplies, storing up general talent, and selecting frontier officials.

sentences.zh: 末言：「以肅皇帝之精明，而末年貪黜成風，封疆多事，則倦勤故也。

translations.literal: At the end he said: 'With the Jiajing emperor's keen intelligence, yet in his later years greed and dismissal became the fashion and the frontiers were full of trouble—that was because of weariness in diligence.
translations.idiomatic: At the end he said: 'With the Jiajing emperor's keen intelligence, yet in his later years greed and dismissal became the fashion and the frontiers were full of trouble—that was because of weariness in diligence.

sentences.zh: 今至尊端拱，百職不修，不亟圖更始，後將安極。」

translations.literal: Now the sovereign sits in dignified repose while the hundred offices go unreformed; if we do not urgently plan a new beginning, where will it end?
translations.idiomatic: Now the sovereign sits in dignified repose while the hundred offices go unreformed; if we do not urgently plan a new beginning, where will it end?

sentences.zh: 帝優詔答之，而不能用。

translations.literal: The emperor answered with a gracious edict but could not put it into practice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered with a gracious edict but could not put it into practice.

sentences.zh: 帝以軍政失察，斥兩都言官三十餘人。

translations.literal: Because military affairs had been poorly supervised, the emperor dismissed more than thirty censors of the two capitals.
translations.idiomatic: Because military affairs had been poorly supervised, the emperor dismissed more than thirty censors of the two capitals.

sentences.zh: 于陛與同官申救至再，又獨疏請宥，俱不納。

translations.literal: Yubi and his colleagues pleaded for mercy twice, and he also submitted a separate memorial asking pardon—all without acceptance.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yubi and his colleagues pleaded for mercy twice, and he also submitted a separate memorial asking pardon—all without acceptance.

sentences.zh: 以甘肅破賊功，加太子少保。

translations.literal: For the merit of defeating bandits in Gansu he was made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: For the merit of defeating bandits in Gansu he was made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 乾清、坤寧兩宮災，請面對，不報。

translations.literal: When the Qianqing and Kunning palaces suffered fire, he asked for a face-to-face audience—no response.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qianqing and Kunning palaces suffered fire, he asked for a face-to-face audience—no response.

sentences.zh: 乞罷，亦不許。

translations.literal: He begged to resign; this too was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He begged to resign; this too was not granted.

sentences.zh: 其秋，二品三年滿，改文淵閣，進太子太保。

translations.literal: That autumn, when three years in the second rank were complete, he was transferred to the Wenyuan Pavilion and promoted to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, when three years in the second rank were complete, he was transferred to the Wenyuan Pavilion and promoted to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 時內閣四人。

translations.literal: At the time there were four men in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there were four men in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 趙誌臯、張位、沈一貫皆于陛同年生，遇事無齟齬。

translations.literal: Zhao Zhigao, Zhang Wei, and Shen Yiguan were all Yubi's classmates in the same examination year; in affairs they had no friction.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhigao, Zhang Wei, and Shen Yiguan were all Chen Yubi's classmates in the same examination year; in affairs they had no friction.

sentences.zh: 而帝拒諫益甚，上下否隔。

translations.literal: But the emperor rejected remonstrance all the more, and above and below were blocked off from one another.
translations.idiomatic: But the emperor rejected remonstrance all the more, and ruler and ministers were blocked off from one another.

sentences.zh: 于陛憂形於色，以不能補救，在直廬數太息視日影。

translations.literal: Yubi's distress showed in his face; because he could not remedy matters, in the duty lodge he would often sigh deeply and watch the sun's shadow.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yubi's distress showed in his face; because he could not remedy matters, in the duty lodge he would often sigh deeply and watch the sun's shadow.

sentences.zh: 二十四年冬，病卒於位，史亦竟罷。

translations.literal: In the winter of the twenty-fourth year he died of illness in office, and the history project was also abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of 1596 he died of illness in office, and the history project was also abandoned.

sentences.zh: 贈少保，謚文憲。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Junior Mentor and given the posthumous title Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Junior Mentor and given the posthumous title Wenxian.

sentences.zh: 終明世，父子為宰輔者，惟南充陳氏。

translations.literal: Through the entire Ming, only the Chen family of Nanchong had father and son serve as chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Through the entire Ming, only the Chen family of Nanchong had father and son serve as chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 世以比漢韋、平焉。

translations.literal: The age compared them to the Han Weis and Pings.
translations.idiomatic: The age compared them to the Han Weis and Pings.

sentences.zh: 沈鯉，字仲化，歸德人。

translations.literal: Shen Li, style name Zhonghua, was a native of Guide.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Li, whose style name was Zhonghua, came from Guide.

sentences.zh: 祖瀚，建寧知府。

translations.literal: His grandfather Han was prefect of Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Han was prefect of Jianning.

sentences.zh: 鯉，嘉靖中舉鄉試。

translations.literal: Li passed the provincial examination in the Jiajing reign.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Li passed the provincial examination in the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 師尚詔作亂，陷歸德，已而西去。

translations.literal: Shi Shangzhao rebelled, took Guide, and then went west.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Shangzhao rebelled, took Guide, and then marched west.

sentences.zh: 鯉策賊必再至，急白守臣，捕殺城中通賊者，嚴為守具。

translations.literal: Li calculated that the bandits would certainly return, urgently informed the defending officials, arrested and killed those in the city who communicated with the bandits, and made strict defensive preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Li calculated that the bandits would certainly return, urgently informed the defending officials, arrested and killed those in the city who communicated with the bandits, and made strict defensive preparations.

sentences.zh: 賊還逼，見有備，去。

translations.literal: The bandits returned and pressed the city; seeing preparations in place, they left.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits returned and pressed the city; seeing preparations in place, they left.

sentences.zh: 奸人倡言屠城，將驅掠居民，鯉請諭止之，眾始定。

translations.literal: Wicked men spread talk of slaughtering the city and were about to drive off and plunder the inhabitants; Li asked that they be instructed to stop, and the multitude was then calmed.
translations.idiomatic: Wicked men spread talk of slaughtering the city and were about to drive off and plunder the inhabitants; Shen Li asked that they be instructed to stop, and the multitude was then calmed.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，成進士，改庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year he became a jinshi, was transferred to Hanlin bachelor, and appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In 1565 he passed the metropolitan examination, was chosen for the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and made a reviser.

sentences.zh: 大學士高拱，其座主又鄉人也，旅見外，未嘗以私謁。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Gao Gong was both his examination patron and a fellow townsman; beyond formal visits on journeys he never called on him privately.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Gao Gong was both his examination patron and a fellow townsman; beyond formal visits on journeys he never called on him privately.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，擢侍講學士，再遷禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: The next autumn he was promoted to lecturer-in-waiting and again transferred to Right Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn he was promoted to lecturer-in-waiting and again transferred to Right Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 尋改吏部，進左侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel and promoted to Left Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel and promoted to Left Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 屏絕私交，好推轂賢士，不使知。

translations.literal: He shut out private connections and loved to advance worthy men without letting them know.
translations.idiomatic: He shut out private connections and loved to advance worthy men without letting them know.

sentences.zh: 十二年冬，拜禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the winter of the twelfth year he was appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of 1584 he was appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 去六品甫二年，至正卿。

translations.literal: Only two years from the sixth rank he reached chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Only two years from the sixth rank he reached chief minister.

sentences.zh: 素負物望，時論不以為驟。

translations.literal: He had long borne public esteem, and contemporary opinion did not regard this as sudden.
translations.idiomatic: He had long borne public esteem, and contemporary opinion did not regard this as sudden.

sentences.zh: 久之，《會典》成，加太子少保。

translations.literal: After a long time, when the Collected Statutes were completed, he was made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time, when the Collected Statutes were completed, he was made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 鯉初官翰林，中官黃錦緣同鄉以幣交，拒不納。

translations.literal: When Li first served in the Hanlin, the eunuch Huang Jin, being a fellow townsman, sought to befriend him with gifts; he refused to accept.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Li first served in the Hanlin, the eunuch Huang Jin, being a fellow townsman, sought to befriend him with gifts; he refused to accept.

sentences.zh: 教習內書堂，侍講筵，皆數與巨珰接，未嘗與交。

translations.literal: In instructing the Inner Writing Hall and attending the lecture mat he often had contact with great eunuchs but never formed connections with them.
translations.idiomatic: In instructing the Inner Writing Hall and attending the lecture mat he often had contact with great eunuchs but never formed connections with them.

sentences.zh: 及官愈高，益無所假借，雖上命及政府指，不徇也。

translations.literal: As his office grew higher he yielded to nothing; even imperial orders and government instructions he would not follow against his judgment.
translations.idiomatic: As his office grew higher he yielded to nothing; even imperial orders and government instructions he would not follow against his judgment.

sentences.zh: 十四年春，貴妃鄭氏生子，進封皇貴妃。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourteenth year the honored consort of the Zheng clan bore a son and was advanced to Imperial Honored Consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1586 the honored consort of the Zheng clan bore a son and was advanced to Imperial Honored Consort.

sentences.zh: 鯉率僚屬請冊建皇長子，進封其母，不許。

translations.literal: Li led his subordinates in asking to invest and establish the eldest imperial son and advance his mother—this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Li led his subordinates in asking to invest and establish the eldest imperial son and advance his mother—this was not granted.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復以為言，且請宥建儲貶官姜應麟等。

translations.literal: Before long he spoke on this again and also asked pardon for those demoted over establishing the heir, such as Jiang Yinglin.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he spoke on this again and also asked pardon for those demoted over establishing the heir, such as Jiang Yinglin.

sentences.zh: 忤旨譙讓。

translations.literal: He offended the imperial will and was rebuked and reproached.
translations.idiomatic: He offended the imperial will and was rebuked and reproached.

sentences.zh: 帝既卻群臣請，因詔諭少俟二三年。

translations.literal: The emperor having rejected the court's request, issued an edict saying to wait a little two or three years.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor having rejected the court's request, issued an edict saying to wait another two or three years.

sentences.zh: 至十六年，期已屆，鯉執前旨固請，帝復不從。

translations.literal: By the sixteenth year the term had arrived; Li held to the earlier instruction and pressed firmly, but the emperor again did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: By 1588 the term had arrived; Shen Li held to the earlier instruction and pressed firmly, but the emperor again did not comply.

sentences.zh: 鯉素鯁亮。

translations.literal: Li was by nature upright and bright.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Li was by nature upright and bright.

sentences.zh: 其在部持典禮，多所建白。

translations.literal: In his ministry he upheld ritual and made many proposals.
translations.idiomatic: In his ministry he upheld ritual and made many proposals.

sentences.zh: 念時俗侈靡，稽先朝典制，自喪祭、冠婚、宮室、器服率定為中制，頒天下。

translations.literal: Mindful that current custom was extravagant, he consulted the institutions of earlier reigns and from mourning sacrifices, capping and marriage, palaces, and vessels and dress set a moderate standard for all and promulgated it throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful that current custom was extravagant, he consulted the institutions of earlier reigns and from mourning sacrifices, capping and marriage, palaces, and vessels and dress set a moderate standard for all and promulgated it throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 又以士習不端，奏行學政八事。

translations.literal: Because scholar-official practice was not upright, he memorialized and put into effect eight items of educational administration.
translations.idiomatic: Because scholar-official practice was not upright, he memorialized and put into effect eight items of educational administration.

sentences.zh: 又請復建文年號，重定《景帝實錄》，勿稱郕戾王。

translations.literal: He also asked to restore the Jianwen reign title, revise the Veritable Records of Emperor Jing, and not call him the Deposed Prince of Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to restore the Jianwen reign title, revise the Veritable Records of Emperor Jing, and not call him the Deposed Prince of Cheng.

sentences.zh: 大同巡撫胡來貢議移祀北嶽渾源，力駁其無據。

translations.literal: The Datong grand coordinator Hu Laigong proposed moving sacrifice to the Northern Peak at Hunyuan; Li forcefully refuted this as groundless.
translations.idiomatic: The Datong grand coordinator Hu Laigong proposed moving sacrifice to the Northern Peak at Hunyuan; Shen Li forcefully refuted this as groundless.

sentences.zh: 太廟侑享，請移親王及諸功臣於兩廡，毋與帝後雜祀。

translations.literal: For secondary offerings in the Imperial Ancestral Temple he asked to move imperial princes and meritorious ministers to the two side halls and not mix their worship with that of emperors and empresses.
translations.idiomatic: For secondary offerings in the Imperial Ancestral Temple he asked to move imperial princes and meritorious ministers to the two side halls and not mix their worship with that of emperors and empresses.

sentences.zh: 進世廟諸妃葬金山者，配食永陵。

translations.literal: He advanced the consorts of the Shizong temple buried at Jinshan to receive offerings at the Yongling.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced the consorts of the Shizong temple buried at Jinshan to receive offerings at the Yongling.

sentences.zh: 諸帝陵祀，請各遣，官毋兼攝。

translations.literal: For sacrifices at the various imperial tombs he asked that each be sent its own official and that offices not hold concurrent appointments.
translations.idiomatic: For sacrifices at the various imperial tombs he asked that each be sent its own official and that offices not hold concurrent appointments.

sentences.zh: 諸王及妃墳祝版稱謂未協者，率請裁定。

translations.literal: Where the prayer-board titles for princes and consorts' tombs were not harmonious, he generally asked that they be decided.
translations.idiomatic: Where the prayer-board titles for princes and consorts' tombs were not harmonious, he generally asked that they be decided.

sentences.zh: 帝憂旱，步禱郊壇，議分遣大臣禱天下名山大川。

translations.literal: The emperor, troubled by drought, walked in prayer at the suburban altar; it was proposed to send great ministers in divisions to pray at famous mountains and great rivers throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, troubled by drought, walked in prayer at the suburban altar; it was proposed to send great ministers in divisions to pray at famous mountains and great rivers throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 鯉言使臣往來驛騷，恐重困民，請齋三日，以告文授太常屬致之，罷寺觀勿禱，帝多可其奏。

translations.literal: Li said that envoys coming and going would disturb the post stations and likely burden the people again; he asked to fast three days, entrust the prayer text to a subordinate of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to deliver it, and stop prayers at temples and monasteries—the emperor approved most of his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Li said that envoys coming and going would disturb the post stations and likely burden the people again; he asked to fast three days, entrust the prayer text to a subordinate of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to deliver it, and stop prayers at temples and monasteries—the emperor approved most of his memorial.

sentences.zh: 鄭貴妃父成憲為父請恤，援後父永年伯例，鯉力駁之。

translations.literal: The father of the Zheng honored consort, Cheng Xian, asked mourning benefits for his father, citing the precedent of the Yongnian marquis, father of an empress; Li forcefully refuted this.
translations.idiomatic: The father of the Zheng honored consort, Cheng Xian, asked mourning benefits for his father, citing the precedent of the Yongnian marquis, father of an empress; Shen Li forcefully refuted this.

sentences.zh: 詔畀葬資五千金，鯉復言過濫。

translations.literal: An edict granted five thousand taels of gold for burial expenses; Li again said this was excessive.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted five thousand taels of gold for burial expenses; Shen Li again said this was excessive.

sentences.zh: 順義王妻三娘子請封，鯉不予妃號，但稱夫人。

translations.literal: The wife of the Prince of Shunyi, the Third Lady, asked for enfeoffment; Li did not grant her the title of consort but only called her Lady.
translations.idiomatic: The wife of the Prince of Shunyi, the Third Lady, asked for enfeoffment; Shen Li did not grant her the title of consort but only called her Lady.

sentences.zh: 真人張國祥言肅皇享國久長，由虔奉玄修所致，勸帝效之，鯉劾國祥詆誣導諛，請正刑辟。

translations.literal: The Perfected Man Zhang Guoxiang said the Jiajing emperor enjoyed a long reign because of devout cultivation of the Mysteries and urged the emperor to imitate this; Li impeached Guoxiang for slander, deception, and leading flattery and asked that proper punishment be applied.
translations.idiomatic: The Perfected Man Zhang Guoxiang said the Jiajing emperor enjoyed a long reign because of devout cultivation of the Mysteries and urged the emperor to imitate this; Shen Li impeached Guoxiang for slander, deception, and leading flattery and asked that proper punishment be applied.

sentences.zh: 事亦寢。

translations.literal: The matter was also shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was also shelved.

sentences.zh: 秦王誼璟故由中尉入繼，而乞封其弟郡王，中貴為請，申時行助之，鯉不可。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin, Yi Jing, had originally entered the succession from a commandery prince rank and now asked to enfeoff his younger brother as Prince of a Commandery; a eunuch pleaded for this and Shen Shixing supported it—Li would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin, Yi Jing, had originally entered the succession from a commandery prince rank and now asked to enfeoff his younger brother as Prince of a Commandery; a eunuch pleaded for this and Shen Shixing supported it—Shen Li would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 唐府違帛請封妾子，執不從，帝並以特旨許之。

translations.literal: The house of Tang sent silk in violation of regulations asking to enfeoff a son by a concubine; he held firm and would not comply, but the emperor permitted it by special edict as well.
translations.idiomatic: The house of Tang sent silk in violation of regulations asking to enfeoff a son by a concubine; he held firm and would not comply, but the emperor permitted it by special edict as well.

sentences.zh: 京師久旱，鯉備陳恤民實政以崇儉戒奢為本，且請減織造。

translations.literal: The capital had long suffered drought; Li fully set forth policies to relieve the people, taking reverence for frugality and warning against extravagance as the foundation, and also asked to reduce weaving and manufacture.
translations.idiomatic: The capital had long suffered drought; Shen Li fully set forth policies to relieve the people, taking reverence for frugality and warning against extravagance as the foundation, and also asked to reduce weaving and manufacture.

sentences.zh: 已，京師地震，又請謹天若戒，恤民窮。

translations.literal: Later, when the capital suffered an earthquake, he again asked to heed heaven's warnings and relieve the people's distress.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the capital suffered an earthquake, he again asked to heed heaven's warnings and relieve the people's distress.

sentences.zh: 畿輔大侵，請上下交修，詞甚切。

translations.literal: The capital region suffered severe famine; he asked that both above and below jointly cultivate rectitude—the language was very urgent.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital region suffered severe famine, he pleaded that ruler and subjects alike must mend their ways; his language was deeply urgent.

sentences.zh: 帝以四方災，敕廷臣修省，鯉因請大損供億營建，振救小民。

translations.literal: The emperor, because of disasters in all quarters, ordered court officials to cultivate rectitude; Li thereupon asked greatly to reduce provisions and construction, and to relieve and save the common people.
translations.idiomatic: When disasters struck across the realm, the emperor ordered the court to undertake moral self-examination; Shen Li seized the moment to urge steep cuts in palace provisioning and building projects and relief for the common people.

sentences.zh: 帝每嘉納。

translations.literal: The emperor each time praised and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consistently praised and accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 初，藩府有所奏請，賄中貴居間，禮臣不敢違，輒如誌。

translations.literal: At first, when princely households had memorial requests, they bribed eunuchs to act as intermediaries; ritual officials did not dare disobey and always granted them as desired.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier times, whenever princely households submitted petitions, they bribed eunuchs to intercede, and the officials of rites dared not refuse—they invariably approved whatever was asked.

sentences.zh: 至鯉，一切格之，中貴皆大怨，數以事間於帝。

translations.literal: When it came to Li, he rejected everything; the eunuchs all greatly resented him and repeatedly set matters before the emperor to sow discord.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Li blocked every such request; the eunuchs loathed him and repeatedly whispered against him to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝漸不能無疑，累加詰責，且奪其俸。

translations.literal: The emperor gradually could not be without suspicion; he repeatedly added interrogations and reproaches, and even confiscated his salary.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gradually grew suspicious, repeatedly reprimanded him, and even withheld his salary.

sentences.zh: 鯉自是有去志。

translations.literal: From this Li had the intent to leave.
translations.idiomatic: From that point Shen Li resolved to resign.

sentences.zh: 而時行銜鯉不附己，亦忌之。

translations.literal: Moreover, Shixing resented that Li did not attach himself to him and also was jealous of him.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Shixing, resenting Shen Li's refusal to align with him, also came to fear and dislike him.

sentences.zh: 一日，鯉請告，遽擬旨放歸。

translations.literal: One day Li asked leave; Shixing immediately drafted an edict sending him home.
translations.idiomatic: One day Shen Li requested leave, and Shixing at once drafted an edict dismissing him.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「沈尚書好官，奈何使去？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Minister Shen is a good official—why send him away?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Minister Shen is an excellent official—why let him go?"

sentences.zh: 傳旨諭留。

translations.literal: An edict was transmitted ordering him to stay.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was sent ordering him to remain in office.

sentences.zh: 時行益忌。

translations.literal: Shixing grew all the more jealous.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Shixing's jealousy only deepened.

sentences.zh: 其私人給事中陳與郊為人求考官不得，怨鯉，屬其同官陳尚象劾之。

translations.literal: His intimate, the supervising secretary Chen Yujiao, failed to obtain an examining official for someone on another's behalf and resented Li; he instructed his colleague Chen Shangxiang to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: His protégé, supervising secretary Chen Yujiao, had failed to secure an examining official for a petitioner and blamed Shen Li; he urged his colleague Chen Shangxiang to impeach him.

sentences.zh: 與郊復危言撼鯉，鯉求去益力。

translations.literal: Yujiao again used alarming words to shake Li; Li sought to leave all the more vigorously.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yujiao piled on with inflammatory accusations; Shen Li pressed all the harder to resign.

sentences.zh: 帝有意大用鯉，微言：「沈尚書不曉人意。」

translations.literal: The emperor had the intent to greatly employ Li and said subtly: "Minister Shen does not understand people's intentions."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still meant to promote Shen Li and remarked pointedly, "Minister Shen does not grasp what people mean."

sentences.zh: 有老宮人從子為內豎者，走告鯉；

translations.literal: An old palace woman's nephew, who was an inner attendant, ran to inform Li;
translations.idiomatic: An elderly palace woman's nephew, serving as an inner attendant, hurried to tell Shen Li;

sentences.zh: 司禮張誠亦屬鯉鄉人內豎廖某密告之。

translations.literal: the Director of Ceremonial Zhang Cheng also instructed an inner attendant surnamed Liao, a fellow townsman of Li, secretly to inform him.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Ceremonial Zhang Cheng likewise asked a fellow townsman of Shen Li's, an inner attendant named Liao, to pass the message in secret.

sentences.zh: 鯉並拒之，曰：「禁中語，非所敢聞。」

translations.literal: Li rejected both, saying: "Words within the forbidden precincts—what dare I hear?"
translations.idiomatic: Shen Li refused them both, saying, "Palace talk is not something I dare to hear."

sentences.zh: 皆恚而去。

translations.literal: All left in anger.
translations.idiomatic: They departed in fury.

sentences.zh: 鯉卒屢疏引疾歸。

translations.literal: Li finally submitted repeated memorials citing illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Li finally submitted repeated memorials pleading illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 累推內閣及吏部尚書，皆不用。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly recommended for the Grand Secretariat and the Ministry of Personnel—neither appointment was used.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly nominated for the Grand Secretariat and for Minister of Personnel, but the emperor appointed neither post to him.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，起南京禮部尚書，辭弗就。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was recalled as Minister of Rites at Nanjing; he declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Wanli he was recalled as Nanjing Minister of Rites, but he declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，趙志臯卒，沈一貫獨當國。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year Zhao Zhigao died; Shen Yiguan alone held the government.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year Zhao Zhigao died, leaving Shen Yiguan sole head of government.

sentences.zh: 廷推閣臣，詔鯉以故官兼東閣大學士，入參機務，與朱賡並命。

translations.literal: The court recommended Grand Secretaries; an edict ordered Li, in his former office, also to serve as Eastern Pavilion Grand Secretary, entering to take part in state affairs—he was appointed together with Zhu Geng.
translations.idiomatic: When the court recommended candidates for the Grand Secretariat, an edict appointed Shen Li, retaining his previous rank, as Eastern Pavilion Grand Secretary to enter and assist in state affairs—he was appointed alongside Zhu Geng.

sentences.zh: 屢辭不允。

translations.literal: He repeatedly declined; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He declined repeatedly, but the emperor would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 明年七月始入朝，時年七十有一矣。

translations.literal: The next year, in the seventh month, he first entered court audience—he was then seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: He did not enter court until the seventh month of the following year, by which time he was seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 一貫以士心夙附鯉，深忌之，貽書李三才曰：「歸德公來，必奪吾位，將何以備之？」

translations.literal: Yiguan, because scholar-officials' hearts had long attached to Li, deeply feared him; he sent a letter to Li Sancai saying: "When the Lord of Guide comes, he will surely seize my position—how am I to guard against it?"
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yiguan, knowing that scholars had long favored Shen Li, deeply resented him and wrote to Li Sancai: "When the Lord of Guide arrives, he will surely take my place—how should I prepare?"

sentences.zh: 歸德，鯉邑名，欲諷鯉辭召命也。

translations.literal: Guide was Li's district name—he meant to urge Li to decline the summons.
translations.idiomatic: Guide was Shen Li's home district—Yiguan meant to suggest that Shen Li refuse the appointment.

sentences.zh: 三才答書，言鯉忠實無他腸，勸一貫同心。

translations.literal: Sancai replied in a letter, saying Li was loyal and sincere without other designs, and urged Yiguan to work with one heart.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sancai replied that Shen Li was loyal and straightforward, and urged Shen Yiguan to cooperate in good faith.

sentences.zh: 一貫由此並憾三才。

translations.literal: Yiguan from this also resented Sancai.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yiguan henceforth resented Li Sancai as well.

sentences.zh: 鯉既至，即具陳道中所見礦稅之害。

translations.literal: Once Li arrived, he immediately set forth in detail the harms of mining taxes he had seen on the road.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as Shen Li arrived, he laid out in full the harm mining levies were doing, as he had witnessed along the way.

sentences.zh: 他日復與賡疏論。

translations.literal: On another day he again memorialized together with Geng.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion he joined Zhu Geng in submitting a memorial on the subject.

sentences.zh: 皆弗納。

translations.literal: All were not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Neither memorial was accepted.

sentences.zh: 楚假王被訐事起，禮部侍郎郭正域請行勘，鯉是之。

translations.literal: When the affair of the pretender king of Chu being denounced arose, Vice Minister of Rites Guo Zhengyu asked that an investigation be conducted; Li agreed.
translations.idiomatic: When the case of the alleged pretender to the Chu princely line arose, Vice Minister of Rites Guo Zhengyu urged a formal inquiry, and Shen Li supported him.

sentences.zh: 及奸人所撰《續憂危竑議》發，一貫輩張皇其事，令其黨錢夢臯誣奏正域、鯉門生，協造妖言，並羅織鯉奸贓數事。

translations.literal: When the "Continued Discussion of Anxiety and Peril in the Heir's Establishment" written by wicked men was exposed, Yiguan's faction magnified the affair, had their partisan Qian Menggao falsely memorialize that Zhengyu and Li's disciples had jointly fabricated sedition, and also fabricated several charges of misconduct and corruption against Li.
translations.idiomatic: When the forged tract Continued Discussion of Anxiety and Peril in the Heir's Establishment came to light, Shen Yiguan's faction sensationalized the case, had his ally Qian Menggao accuse Guo Zhengyu and Shen Li's students of colluding in seditious talk, and fabricated multiple charges of graft against Shen Li as well.

sentences.zh: 帝察其誣，不問。

translations.literal: The emperor perceived it was false accusation and did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw through the frame-up and took no action.

sentences.zh: 而一貫輩使邏卒日夜操兵圍守其邸。

translations.literal: Yet Yiguan's faction sent patrol soldiers day and night bearing arms to surround and guard his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Nevertheless Shen Yiguan's men posted armed patrols day and night around Shen Li's residence.

sentences.zh: 已而事解，復譖鯉詛咒。

translations.literal: Before long the affair was resolved; they again slandered Li for cursing.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair subsided, they accused Shen Li anew of casting curses.

sentences.zh: 鯉嘗置小屏閣中，列書謹天戒、恤民窮、開言路、發章奏、用大僚、補庶官、起廢棄、舉考選、釋冤獄、撤稅使十事，而上書「天啟聖聰，撥亂反治」八字。

translations.literal: Li had once placed a small screen in his pavilion, listing ten matters—in reverence for heaven's warnings, relieving the people's distress, opening avenues of speech, forwarding memorials, employing great officials, filling common offices, raising the discarded, conducting examinations and selections, releasing wrongful prisoners, and withdrawing tax commissioners—and above writing the eight characters "Heaven enlightens the sage's understanding; dispel disorder and restore order."
translations.idiomatic: Shen Li had kept a small screen in his study listing ten reforms—heed heaven's warnings, relieve the people's distress, open avenues of remonstrance, relay memorials promptly, appoint great ministers, fill vacant posts, rehabilitate the disgraced, conduct examinations fairly, release the wrongfully imprisoned, and withdraw mining tax commissioners—and inscribed above them the eight characters: "May Heaven enlighten the sage's understanding and restore order from chaos."

sentences.zh: 每入閣，輒焚香拜祝之，讒者遂指為詛咒。

translations.literal: Each time he entered the Grand Secretariat he would burn incense and bow in prayer to it; slanderers then pointed to this as cursing.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he entered the Grand Secretariat he would burn incense and bow before it; his enemies then claimed he was performing curses.

sentences.zh: 帝取入視之，曰：「此豈詛咒耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor had it brought in to view and said: "How is this cursing?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had the screen brought in and said, "How is this a curse?"

sentences.zh: 讒者曰：「彼詛咒語，固不宣諸口。」

translations.literal: The slanderers said: "Those words of cursing—of course one does not speak them aloud."
translations.idiomatic: His accusers said, "Curse words are not meant to be spoken aloud."

sentences.zh: 賴帝知鯉深，不之信。

translations.literal: Relying on the emperor's deep knowledge of Li, they were not believed.
translations.idiomatic: But the emperor knew Shen Li too well to believe them.

sentences.zh: 先是，閣臣奏揭不輕進，進則無不答者。

translations.literal: Previously, Grand Secretaries' confidential memorials were not lightly submitted; once submitted, there was none unanswered.
