translations.idiomatic: Formerly, confidential memorials from the Grand Secretariat were submitted sparingly, and once submitted were always answered.

sentences.zh: 是時中外扞格，奏揭繁，多寢不下。

translations.literal: At this time court and countryside were at odds; confidential memorials were numerous, and most were shelved without response.
translations.idiomatic: Now court and country were at loggerheads; memorials piled up, and most were left unanswered.

sentences.zh: 鯉以失職，累引疾求退。

translations.literal: Li, considering himself failing in duty, repeatedly cited illness seeking to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Feeling he could no longer perform his duties, Shen Li repeatedly pleaded illness and asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 獎諭有加，卒不能行其所請。

translations.literal: Encouragement and edicts were added, but in the end what he requested could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor showered him with commendations, yet still refused his request to leave.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，敘皮林功，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year, recording the Pilin merit, he was promoted to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year his service in suppressing the Pilin rebellion was rewarded with promotion to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 尋以秩滿，加少保，改文淵閣。

translations.literal: Soon, on completion of his term, he was made Junior Guardian and transferred to the Wenyuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, at the end of his term, he was made Junior Guardian and transferred to Wenyuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 鯉初相，即請除礦稅。

translations.literal: When Li first became chief minister, he immediately asked to abolish mining taxes.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as Shen Li entered the Grand Secretariat, he called for abolishing mining levies.

sentences.zh: 居位數年，數以為言。

translations.literal: In office for several years, he repeatedly spoke on this.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his years in office he raised the issue again and again.

sentences.zh: 會長陵明樓災，鯉語一貫、賡各為奏，俟時上之。

translations.literal: When the Bright Tower at Changling suffered fire, Li told Yiguan and Geng each to prepare a memorial and wait for the time to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When fire damaged the Bright Tower at the Changling mausoleum, Shen Li told Shen Yiguan and Zhu Geng each to draft a memorial and await the right moment to submit it.

sentences.zh: 一日大雨，鯉曰：「可矣。」

translations.literal: One day there was heavy rain; Li said: "It will do."
translations.idiomatic: One rainy day Shen Li said, "Now is the time."

sentences.zh: 兩人問故，鯉曰：「帝惡言礦稅事，疏入多不視，今吾輩冒雨素服詣文華奏之，上訝而取閱，亦一機也。」

translations.literal: The two asked why; Li said: "The emperor dislikes talk of mining taxes; when memorials come in he often does not look at them. Now if we go in rain in plain dress to the Wenhua Gate to submit them, the emperor will be surprised and take them to read—that too is an opportunity."
translations.idiomatic: When they asked why, he said, "The emperor hates hearing about mining levies and often ignores such memorials. If we go now in plain robes through the rain to submit them at the Wenhua Gate, his surprise may make him read them—that is our opening."

sentences.zh: 兩人從其言。

translations.literal: The two followed his words.
translations.idiomatic: The two men did as he advised.

sentences.zh: 帝得疏，曰：「必有急事。」

translations.literal: The emperor received the memorial and said: "There must be urgent business."
translations.idiomatic: Receiving the memorial, the emperor said, "This must be urgent."

sentences.zh: 啟視，果心動，然不為罷。

translations.literal: He opened and looked; his heart was indeed moved, yet he did not abolish them.
translations.idiomatic: He opened it and was indeed moved, but still did not abolish the levies.

sentences.zh: 明年長至，一貫在告，鯉、賡謁賀仁德門。

translations.literal: The next year at the winter solstice, Yiguan was on leave; Li and Geng went to offer felicitations at the Gate of Human Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: At the winter solstice the following year, with Shen Yiguan on leave, Shen Li and Zhu Geng went to offer congratulations at the Gate of Human Virtue.

sentences.zh: 帝賜食，司禮太監陳矩侍，小璫數往來竊聽，且執筆以俟。

translations.literal: The emperor granted food; the Director of Ceremonial eunuch Chen Ju attended; junior eunuchs repeatedly came and went eavesdropping and also held pens waiting.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted them a meal, with Director of Ceremonial Chen Ju in attendance; junior eunuchs shuttled back and forth to eavesdrop, pens in hand to record every word.

sentences.zh: 鯉因極陳礦稅害民狀，矩亦戚然。

translations.literal: Li thereupon fully set forth the condition of mining taxes harming the people; Ju also looked sorrowful.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Li spoke at length about the suffering mining levies inflicted on the people, and Chen Ju looked deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 鯉復進曰：「礦使出，破壞天下名山大川靈氣盡矣，恐於聖躬不利。」

translations.literal: Li again advanced and said: "When mining commissioners go out, they destroy the famous mountains and great rivers of the realm until their spiritual essence is exhausted—this may be unfavorable to Your Majesty's person."
translations.idiomatic: Shen Li added, "When mining commissioners go forth, they ravage the famous mountains and rivers until their vital essence is spent—I fear this bodes ill for Your Majesty's health."

sentences.zh: 矩嘆息還，具為帝道之。

translations.literal: Ju sighed and returned, fully reporting it to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ju sighed and withdrew, then reported everything to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝悚然遣矩諮鯉所以補救者。

translations.literal: The emperor, startled, sent Ju to consult Li on how to remedy it.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, the emperor sent Chen Ju to ask Shen Li what could be done.

sentences.zh: 鯉曰：「此無他，急停開鑿，則靈氣自復。」

translations.literal: Li said: "In this there is nothing else—urgently stop opening and excavating, and the spiritual essence will naturally recover."
translations.idiomatic: Shen Li answered, "There is but one remedy: halt mining at once, and the land's vital essence will restore itself."

sentences.zh: 帝聞，為首肯。

translations.literal: The emperor, hearing this, nodded his head in approval.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nodded in agreement.

sentences.zh: 一貫慮鯉獨收其功，急草疏上。

translations.literal: Yiguan, fearing Li alone would reap the credit, urgently drafted a memorial and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Shen Li alone would win the credit, Shen Yiguan hastily drafted his own memorial.

sentences.zh: 帝不懌，復止。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and again stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased and once again held off acting.

sentences.zh: 然越月果下停礦之命，鯉力也。

translations.literal: Yet crossing a month, the order stopping mining was indeed issued—Li's effort.
translations.idiomatic: Yet within a month the order halting mining levies was indeed issued—thanks to Shen Li.

sentences.zh: 鯉遇事秉正不撓。

translations.literal: In matters Li held to rectitude and did not bend.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Li stood upright and unyielding in every affair.

sentences.zh: 壓於一貫，志不盡行。

translations.literal: Pressed by Yiguan, his aims were not fully carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Checked by Shen Yiguan, he could not fully carry out his aims.

sentences.zh: 而是時一貫數被論，引疾杜門，鯉乃得行閣事。

translations.literal: But at this time Yiguan was repeatedly criticized, cited illness and shut his door; Li then was able to conduct Grand Secretariat business.
translations.idiomatic: But when Shen Yiguan, repeatedly attacked by critics, claimed illness and withdrew, Shen Li was able at last to manage Grand Secretariat affairs himself.

sentences.zh: 皇孫生，詔赦天下。

translations.literal: When the imperial grandson was born, an edict amnestied the realm.
translations.idiomatic: At the birth of the imperial grandson, an edict proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 中官請征茶蠟夙逋，鯉以戾詔旨，再執奏，竟報寢，帝乳母翊聖夫人金氏，其夫官都督同知，歿，請以從子繼。

translations.literal: Eunuchs asked to levy long-overdue tea and wax taxes; Li held that this contravened the edict's intent, repeatedly submitted firmly, and in the end the reply was shelved. The emperor's wet nurse, the Lady of Assisting Sagacity, née Jin—her husband held the office of Vice Commissioner-in-Chief of the Chief Military Commission; when he died, she asked that a nephew succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs sought to collect long-standing arrears on tea and wax levies; Shen Li argued this violated the amnesty and submitted twice in firm protest—the request was shelved. The emperor's wet nurse, Lady Jin of Assisting Sagacity, whose husband had held the post of Vice Commissioner-in-Chief of the Chief Military Commission, asked upon his death that a nephew inherit the rank.

sentences.zh: 鯉言都督非世官，乃已。

translations.literal: Li said that Commissioner-in-Chief posts were not hereditary offices, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Li replied that military commissioner posts were not hereditary, and the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 真人張國祥謂皇孫誕生，己有祝釐功，乞三代誥命且世襲詹事主簿。

translations.literal: The Perfected Man Zhang Guoxiang said that with the imperial grandson's birth he had prayer merit, and asked for patent of nobility for three generations and hereditary appointment as Registrar of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: The Perfected Man Zhang Guoxiang claimed merit for prayers offered at the imperial grandson's birth and asked for patents of nobility extending three generations and a hereditary post as Registrar of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 鯉力斥其謬，乃賚以金幣。

translations.literal: Li forcefully refuted his absurdity; he was then bestowed gold and coins.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Li forcefully rejected the claim; Zhang was given gold and silk instead.

sentences.zh: 帝惑中貴言，將察核畿輔牧地，諭鯉撰敕。

translations.literal: The emperor, swayed by eunuchs' words, was about to investigate and verify pasture lands in the capital region and ordered Li to draft an edict.
translations.idiomatic: Persuaded by eunuchs, the emperor planned an audit of pasture lands in the capital region and ordered Shen Li to draft the edict.

sentences.zh: 鯉言：「近年以來，百利之源，盡籠於朝廷，常恐勢極生變。

translations.literal: Li said: "In recent years, sources of all profit have been entirely gathered into the court; I constantly fear that when power reaches its extreme change will arise.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Li said, "In recent years every source of revenue has been drawn into the court's grasp; I constantly fear that when exploitation reaches its limit, upheaval will follow.

sentences.zh: 況此牧地，豈真有豪右隱占新墾未科者？

translations.literal: Moreover, as for these pasture lands—is it really so that powerful families secretly occupy newly reclaimed land untaxed?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, do these pasture lands truly conceal powerful families squatting on newly reclaimed, untaxed land?

sentences.zh: 奸民所傳，未足深信。」

translations.literal: What wicked commoners spread is not sufficient to be deeply believed."
translations.idiomatic: Such tales come from scheming rumormongers and are not to be trusted."

sentences.zh: 遂止。

translations.literal: The matter was then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 雲南武弁殺稅使楊榮。

translations.literal: A military officer in Yunnan killed the tax commissioner Yang Rong.
translations.idiomatic: A military officer in Yunnan killed the tax commissioner Yang Rong.

sentences.zh: 帝怒甚，將遣官逮治。

translations.literal: The emperor was very angry and was about to dispatch officials to arrest and punish.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and prepared to send officials to apprehend and punish those involved.

sentences.zh: 鯉具陳榮罪狀，請誅為首殺榮者，而貸其餘，乃不果逮。

translations.literal: Li fully set forth Rong's criminal acts, asked to execute those chief in killing Rong and pardon the rest, and thus the arrest did not take place.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Li detailed Yang Rong's crimes, urged execution only for the ringleaders in his killing and leniency for the rest, and the apprehension was not carried out.

sentences.zh: 陜西稅使梁永求領鎮守事，亦以鯉言罷。

translations.literal: The Shaanxi tax commissioner Liang Yong asked to take charge of garrison affairs—it too was stopped on Li's words.
translations.idiomatic: The Shaanxi tax commissioner Liang Yong's bid to assume garrison command was likewise blocked on Shen Li's advice.

sentences.zh: 遼東稅使高淮假進貢名，率所統練甲至國門。

translations.literal: The Liaodong tax commissioner Gao Huai, under the name of presenting tribute, led the trained armored troops under his command to the capital gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Liaodong tax commissioner Gao Huai marched the armed troops under his command to the capital gates under the pretext of delivering tribute.

sentences.zh: 鯉中夜密奏其不可，詔責淮而止。

translations.literal: Li at midnight secretly memorialized that this could not be allowed; an edict reprimanded Huai and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Li submitted a secret midnight memorial protesting the move; the emperor rebuked Gao Huai and ordered him to stop.

sentences.zh: 時一貫雖稱疾杜門，而章奏多即家擬旨，鯉力言非故事。

translations.literal: At this time although Yiguan claimed illness and shut his door, memorials and edicts were mostly drafted at his home; Li forcefully said this was not precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Though Shen Yiguan claimed illness and stayed home, he continued drafting edicts from his residence; Shen Li insisted this violated precedent.

sentences.zh: 鯉既積忤一貫，一貫將去，慮鯉在，貽己後憂欲與俱去，密傾之。

translations.literal: Li had accumulated offenses against Yiguan; as Yiguan was about to leave, fearing that if Li remained he would leave trouble for himself afterward and wanting to leave together with him, he secretly undermined him.
translations.idiomatic: Having long crossed Shen Yiguan, Shen Yiguan—as he prepared to retire—feared Shen Li would remain and cause him trouble afterward; wishing to take Shen Li with him, he secretly worked against him.

sentences.zh: 帝亦嫌鯉方鯁，因鯉乞休，遽命與一貫同致仕。

translations.literal: The emperor also disliked Li's uncompromising squareness; when Li asked to retire, he immediately ordered him to retire together with Yiguan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor likewise resented Shen Li's stubborn rectitude; when Shen Li asked to retire, he promptly ordered him to leave office together with Shen Yiguan.

sentences.zh: 賡疏乞留鯉，不報。

translations.literal: Geng memorialized asking to retain Li—no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Geng memorialized asking that Shen Li be kept on—there was no response.

sentences.zh: 既抵家，疏謝，猶極陳怠政之弊，以明作進規。

translations.literal: Once he reached home, he submitted a memorial of thanks, still fully setting forth the evils of lax governance, using clarity and diligence to advance remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: After reaching home he submitted a memorial of thanks that still laid bare the evils of slack governance, offering frank counsel in the spirit of enlightened rule.

sentences.zh: 年八十，遣官存問，賚銀幣。

translations.literal: At age eighty, officials were dispatched to inquire after him and bestow silver and coins.
translations.idiomatic: At eighty the court sent officials to inquire after his health and bestow silver and silk.

sentences.zh: 鯉奏謝，復陳時政要務。

translations.literal: Li submitted thanks and again set forth important matters of current governance.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Li submitted his thanks and again outlined pressing issues of state.

sentences.zh: 又五年卒，年八十五。

translations.literal: After five more years he died, aged eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Five years later he died, at the age of eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈太師，謚文端。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor and given the posthumous title Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor with the posthumous name Wenduan ("Cultured and Upright").

sentences.zh: 于慎行

translations.literal: Yu Shenxing
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shenxing

sentences.zh: 于慎行，字無垢，東阿人。

translations.literal: Yu Shenxing, style name Wugou, was a native of Dong'e.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shenxing, whose style name was Wugou, came from Dong'e.

sentences.zh: 年十七，舉於鄉。

translations.literal: At age seventeen he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he passed the provincial civil examination.

sentences.zh: 御史欲即鹿鳴宴冠之，以未奉父命辭。

translations.literal: The censor wished immediately at the Lu-Ming banquet to crown him with the cap; he declined because he had not received his father's command.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising censor wished to confer the cap on him at the Lu-Ming banquet, but he declined for lack of his father's permission.

sentences.zh: 隆慶二年成進士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longqing he completed and became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1568 he passed the metropolitan examination and received his jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be a Hanlin bachelor and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a Hanlin bachelor and appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 萬曆初，《穆宗實錄》成，進修撰，充日講官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wanli, when the Veritable Records of Emperor Muzong were completed, he was promoted to senior compiler and appointed a daily lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wanli reign, after the Veritable Records of the Longqing Emperor were finished, he was promoted to senior compiler and assigned as a daily lecturer at court.

sentences.zh: 故事，率以翰林大僚值日講，無及史官者。

translations.literal: According to precedent, daily lecturers were generally senior Hanlin officials; none had ever been drawn from among the historiographers.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, daily lecturers were usually drawn from the senior ranks of the Hanlin Academy—historiographers had never held the post.

sentences.zh: 慎行與張位及王家屏、沈一貫、陳于陛咸以史官得之，異也。

translations.literal: Shenxing, together with Zhang Wei as well as Wang Jiabing, Shen Yiguan, and Chen Yubi, all obtained the post as historiographers—an anomaly.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxing, along with Zhang Wei, Wang Jiabing, Shen Yiguan, and Chen Yubi, all received the appointment despite being historiographers—a departure from precedent.

sentences.zh: 嘗講罷，帝出御府圖畫，令講官分題。

translations.literal: Once, after a lecture session ended, the emperor brought out paintings from the imperial collection and had the lecturers each take a subject.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion, after a lecture, the emperor produced paintings from the imperial collection and asked each lecturer to compose on an assigned theme.

sentences.zh: 慎行不善書，詩成，屬人書之，具以實對。

translations.literal: Shenxing was not skilled at calligraphy; when his poem was finished, he had someone else write it out and reported the facts fully to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxing was a poor calligrapher, so once his poem was done he had someone else copy it out and told the emperor plainly what he had done.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，嘗大書「責難陳善」四字賜之，詞林傳為盛事。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and once wrote in large characters the four words "Pressing for difficulty and presenting what is good" as a gift to him; the Hanlin Academy spread word of it as a great occasion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and once bestowed on him a large inscription of the four characters "Pressing for difficulty and presenting what is good"—a gift the Hanlin Academy long celebrated as a signal honor.

sentences.zh: 御史劉臺以劾張居正被逮，僚友悉避匿，慎行獨往視之。

translations.literal: Censor Liu Tai was arrested for impeaching Zhang Juzheng; colleagues all avoided and hid themselves, but Shenxing alone went to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: When Censor Liu Tai was arrested for impeaching Zhang Juzheng, his colleagues all kept their distance, but Shenxing alone went to see him.

sentences.zh: 及居正奪情，偕同官具疏諫。

translations.literal: When Juzheng took leave from mourning contrary to custom, he joined his fellow officials in drafting a memorial of remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Juzheng declined to leave office to mourn his father, Shenxing joined his colleagues in submitting a memorial of protest.

sentences.zh: 呂調陽格之，不得上。

translations.literal: Lü Diaoyang blocked it, and it could not be submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Diaoyang intercepted the memorial, and it never reached the throne.

sentences.zh: 居正聞而怒，他日謂慎行曰：「子吾所厚，亦為此耶？」

translations.literal: Juzheng heard of it and grew angry; another day he said to Shenxing, "You are one I have treated well—would you also do this?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juzheng heard of it and was furious. On another day he said to Shenxing, "I have always favored you—would you do this too?"

sentences.zh: 慎行從容對曰：「正以公見厚故耳。」

translations.literal: Shenxing calmly replied, "It is precisely because you have treated me well."
translations.idiomatic: Shenxing answered calmly, "It is precisely because you have shown me such favor."

sentences.zh: 居正怫然。

translations.literal: Juzheng was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juzheng was displeased.

sentences.zh: 慎行尋以疾歸。

translations.literal: Before long Shenxing returned home on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shenxing resigned and went home, citing illness.

sentences.zh: 居正卒，起故官。

translations.literal: When Juzheng died, he was recalled to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Juzheng died, Shenxing was recalled to his former post.

sentences.zh: 進左諭德，日講如故。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent and continued as daily lecturer as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent and continued his duties as a daily lecturer.

sentences.zh: 時居正已敗，侍郎丘橓往籍其家。

translations.literal: By then Juzheng had already fallen; Vice Minister Qiu Zhen went to register and seize his household property.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zhang Juzheng had already fallen from power, and Vice Minister Qiu Zhen was sent to inventory and seize his family's property.

sentences.zh: 慎行遺書，言居正母老，諸子覆巢之下，顛沛可傷，宜推明主帷蓋恩，全大臣簪履之誼。

translations.literal: Shenxing sent a letter saying that Juzheng's mother was old, that his sons beneath a fallen nest were in pitiable distress, and that one should extend the enlightened ruler's grace of the canopy and cover and preserve the propriety between ruler and minister as of cap and shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxing wrote to Qiu Zhen, noting that Zhang Juzheng's mother was elderly and his sons, with their household ruined, were in wretched straits; he urged that the emperor's grace be extended to shield the family and that the bond between sovereign and minister be honored to the end.

sentences.zh: 詞極懇摯，時論韙之。

translations.literal: The language was extremely earnest and sincere, and contemporary opinion approved it.
translations.idiomatic: His words were deeply earnest, and public opinion applauded him.

sentences.zh: 由侍講學士擢禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: From Lecturer-in-Waiting he was elevated to Right Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted from Lecturer-in-Waiting to Right Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 轉左，改吏部，掌詹事府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the left vice ministership, moved to the Ministry of Personnel, and directed the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the left vice ministership, reassigned to the Ministry of Personnel, and put in charge of the Household of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 尋遷禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to be Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 慎行明習典制，諸大禮多所裁定。

translations.literal: Shenxing was well versed in statutes and institutions and adjudicated many major ritual matters.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxing was thoroughly versed in ritual law and settled many major ceremonial disputes.

sentences.zh: 先是，嘉靖中孝烈後升祔，祧仁宗。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Jiajing reign, when Empress Xiaolie was enshrined by secondary placement, Emperor Renzong was displaced from the temple.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Jiajing reign, when Empress Xiaolie was enshrined in the imperial temple, Emperor Renzong was removed from his place.

sentences.zh: 萬曆改元，穆宗升祔，復祧宣宗。

translations.literal: When Wanli changed the reign title, Emperor Muzong was enshrined by secondary placement, and Emperor Xuanzong was again displaced from the temple.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Wanli reign, when Emperor Muzong was enshrined in the temple, Emperor Xuanzong was displaced in turn.

sentences.zh: 慎行謂非禮，作《太廟祧遷考》，言：「古七廟之制，三昭三穆，與太祖之廟而七。

translations.literal: Shenxing held that this was not according to ritual and wrote An Inquiry into the Displacement and Transfer in the Grand Ancestral Temple, saying: "The ancient system of seven temples comprised three zhao and three mu, together with the temple of the founding ancestor, making seven.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxing argued that this violated ritual propriety and wrote An Inquiry into Ancestral Temple Displacement, stating: "The ancient system of seven temples consisted of three zhao and three mu, together with the founding ancestor's shrine, for seven in all.

sentences.zh: 劉歆、王肅並以高、曾、祖、禰及五世、六世為三昭三穆。

translations.literal: Liu Xin and Wang Su both took the great-great-grandfather, great-grandfather, grandfather, and father, together with the fifth and sixth generations, as the three zhao and three mu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin and Wang Su both understood the three zhao and three mu to comprise the great-great-grandfather, great-grandfather, grandfather, and father, along with the fifth and sixth generations.

sentences.zh: 其兄弟相傳，則同堂異室，不可為一世。

translations.literal: Where brothers succeeded one another, they shared the same hall but had separate chambers and could not count as one generation.
translations.idiomatic: When the throne passed between brothers, they shared one hall but occupied separate chambers and could not be counted as a single generation.

sentences.zh: 國朝成祖既為世室，與太祖俱百世不遷，則仁宗以下，必實歷六世，而後三昭三穆始備。

translations.literal: In our dynasty, since Emperor Chengzu was made the perpetual shrine and he and the founding ancestor are both never displaced for a hundred generations, then from Emperor Renzong downward there must in fact be six generations before the three zhao and three mu are complete.
translations.idiomatic: In our dynasty, since the Yongle Emperor was made the perpetual shrine and he and the founding emperor are both never displaced, there must be six actual generations from the Hongxi Emperor downward before the three zhao and three mu are complete.

sentences.zh: 孝宗與睿宗兄弟，武宗與世宗兄弟，韶穆同，不當各為一世。

translations.literal: Emperors Xiaozong and Ruizong were brothers, and Emperors Wuzong and Shizong were brothers; their zhao and mu positions were the same, and they ought not each to count as one generation.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongzhi Emperor and Ruizong were brothers, as were the Zhengde and Jiajing Emperors; their zhao and mu positions were identical, and they should not each be counted as separate generations.

sentences.zh: 世宗升，距仁宗止六世，不當祧仁宗。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong was enshrined, there were only six generations from Emperor Renzong; Renzong ought not to have been displaced.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiajing Emperor was enshrined, only six generations had passed since the Hongxi Emperor; the Hongxi Emperor should not have been displaced.

sentences.zh: 穆宗升祔，當祧仁宗，不當祧宣宗。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong was enshrined by secondary placement, Emperor Renzong should have been displaced, not Emperor Xuanzong."
translations.idiomatic: When the Longqing Emperor was enshrined, the Hongxi Emperor should have been displaced—not the Xuande Emperor."

sentences.zh: 引晉、唐、宋故事為據，其言辨而核。

translations.literal: He cited precedents from the Jin, Tang, and Song as evidence; his argument was discriminating and exact.
translations.idiomatic: He cited Jin, Tang, and Song precedents in support, and his argument was precise and well substantiated.

sentences.zh: 事雖不行，識者服其知禮。

translations.literal: Although the proposal was not adopted, those who understood the matter admired his knowledge of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Although his proposal was not adopted, informed opinion respected his mastery of ritual.

sentences.zh: 又言：「南昌、壽春等十六王，世次既遠，宜別祭陵園，不宜祔享太廟。」

translations.literal: He also said: "The sixteen princes such as those of Nanchang and Shouchun, whose generations are already distant, ought to be separately sacrificed at their mausoleum parks and ought not to receive secondary enshrinement in the Grand Ancestral Temple."
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that the sixteen princely lines of Nanchang, Shouchun, and the like, being many generations removed, should be honored at their own mausoleum parks rather than enshrined in the Grand Ancestral Temple."

sentences.zh: 亦寢不行。

translations.literal: This too was shelved and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: This proposal, too, was shelved.

sentences.zh: 十八年正月，疏請早建東宮，出閣講讀。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighteenth year he memorialized requesting that the Eastern Palace be established early and that the heir leave the palace to receive lectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eighteenth year of Wanli he submitted a memorial urging that the heir apparent be formally invested and begin formal study outside the palace.

sentences.zh: 及冬，又請。

translations.literal: When winter came, he petitioned again.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he petitioned again.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，再嚴旨詰責。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and twice issued stern edicts rebuking and questioning him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and twice issued stern edicts rebuking him.

sentences.zh: 慎行不為懾，明日復言：「冊立臣部職掌，臣等不言，罪有所歸。

translations.literal: Shenxing was not intimidated; the next day he spoke again: "Investiture and establishment are the responsibility of my ministry; if we officials do not speak, the guilt will fall somewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxing was undeterred. The next day he wrote again: "Investiture of the heir is this ministry's duty; if we remain silent, the blame will fall on us.

sentences.zh: 幸速決大計，放歸田里。」

translations.literal: I beg that the great decision be made quickly and that I be sent back to my fields and village."
translations.idiomatic: Please settle this great matter at once and allow me to retire to my home."

sentences.zh: 帝益不悅，責以要君疑上，淆亂國本，及僚屬皆奪俸。

translations.literal: The emperor was all the more displeased, rebuked him for coercing the ruler and sowing doubt toward the sovereign and for confusing the foundation of the state, and stripped him and his subordinates of salary.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew still angrier, accusing him of holding the throne hostage, casting doubt on the sovereign, and unsettling the succession—and stripped him and his subordinates of their salaries.

sentences.zh: 山東鄉試，預傳典試者名，已而果然。

translations.literal: In the Shandong provincial examination, the names of the chief examiners were circulated in advance, and afterward it proved true.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shandong provincial examination, the names of the chief examiners were leaked in advance—and the leak proved accurate.

sentences.zh: 言者遂劾禮官，皆停俸。

translations.literal: Critics thereupon impeached the officials of Rites, and all had their salaries suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Critics then impeached the Rites officials, and all of them had their salaries suspended.

sentences.zh: 慎行引罪乞休。

translations.literal: Shenxing acknowledged guilt and requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxing accepted blame and asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 章累上，乃許。

translations.literal: Memorials piled up in submission, and only then was he permitted.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated memorials, the emperor finally granted his request.

sentences.zh: 家居十餘年，中外屢薦，率報寢。

translations.literal: He lived at home for more than ten years; inside and outside the court he was repeatedly recommended, but the reports were generally shelved.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement for more than ten years. Recommendations poured in from inside and outside the court, but they were invariably ignored.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，始起掌詹事府。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he was at last recalled to direct the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year of Wanli he was at last recalled to head the Household of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 疏辭，復留不下。

translations.literal: He memorialized to decline, but was again retained and not released.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial declining the appointment, but the emperor kept him in post.

sentences.zh: 居二年，廷推閣臣七人，首慎行。

translations.literal: After two years in office, seven men were court-recommended as Grand Secretaries, with Shenxing first.
translations.idiomatic: After two years, the court recommended seven men for the Grand Secretariat, with Shenxing ranked first.

sentences.zh: 詔加太子少保兼東閣大學士，入參機務。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and concurrent Eastern Pavilion Grand Secretary, entering to take part in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made him Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Eastern Pavilion Grand Secretary, entrusting him with affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 再辭不允，乃就道。

translations.literal: He declined twice without acceptance and then set out on the road.
translations.idiomatic: He declined twice, but when the emperor would not accept his refusal, he set out for the capital.

sentences.zh: 時慎行已得疾。

translations.literal: By then Shenxing was already ill.
translations.idiomatic: By then Shenxing was already ill.

sentences.zh: 及廷謝，拜起不如儀，上疏請罪。

translations.literal: When he came to court to give thanks, his bowing and rising were not according to protocol; he submitted a memorial requesting punishment.
translations.idiomatic: At his audience of thanks, his bows and movements fell short of proper form, and he submitted a memorial asking to be punished.

sentences.zh: 歸臥於家，遂草遺疏，請帝親大臣、錄遣逸、補言官。

translations.literal: He returned home to lie ill and then drafted a final memorial, asking the emperor to receive ministers personally, record and employ the overlooked and retired, and fill the posts of remonstrating officials.
translations.idiomatic: He went home to his sickbed and drafted a final memorial urging the emperor to meet his ministers in person, recall overlooked talent, and fill the ranks of remonstrating officials.

sentences.zh: 數日卒，年六十三。

translations.literal: Within several days he died, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died a few days later, at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保，謚文定。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous name Wending.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous name Wending.

sentences.zh: 慎行學有原委，貫穿百家。

translations.literal: Shenxing's learning had clear origins and threads, penetrating the hundred schools.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxing's scholarship was deeply grounded and ranged across the full breadth of classical learning.

sentences.zh: 神宗時，詞館中以慎行及臨朐馮琦文學為一時冠。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Shenzong, among the Hanlin Academy Shenxing and Feng Qi of Linqu were regarded as the foremost in literary accomplishment of the age.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign, Shenxing and Feng Qi of Linqu were considered the leading literary figures in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 李廷機

translations.literal: Li Tingji
translations.idiomatic: Li Tingji

sentences.zh: 李廷機，字爾張，晉江人。

translations.literal: Li Tingji, style name Erzhang, was a native of Jinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tingji, whose style name was Erzhang, came from Jinjiang.

sentences.zh: 貢入太學，順天鄉試第一。

translations.literal: He entered the Imperial Academy as a tribute student and placed first in the Shuntian provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Imperial Academy as a tribute student and ranked first in the Shuntian provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十一年，會試復第一，以進土第二授編修。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Wanli he again placed first in the metropolitan examination and, as second-ranked jinshi, was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Wanli he again topped the palace examination and, as second-ranked jinshi, was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 累遷祭酒。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to become Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 故事，祭酒每視事，則二生共舉一牌詣前，大書「整齊嚴肅」四字。

translations.literal: According to precedent, whenever the chancellor took up his duties, two students together would carry a placard before him on which were written in large characters the four words "Orderly, strict, and solemn."
translations.idiomatic: By custom, whenever the chancellor took up his duties, two students would carry before him a placard bearing the four characters "Orderly, strict, and solemn."

sentences.zh: 蓋高皇帝所制，以警師儒者。

translations.literal: This was instituted by the founding emperor as a warning to teachers and scholars.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor had instituted this practice as a reminder to teachers and scholars.

sentences.zh: 廷機見之惕然，故其立教，一以嚴為主。

translations.literal: When Tingji saw it he was awed and vigilant; therefore in establishing his teaching he took strictness as his sole principle.
translations.idiomatic: Tingji was deeply moved when he saw it, and in his teaching he made strictness his guiding principle.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷南京吏部右侍郎，署部事。

translations.literal: After a long time he was transferred to Right Vice Minister of Personnel in Nanjing and directed the ministry's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was transferred to Right Vice Minister of Personnel in Nanjing and placed in charge of the ministry.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，典京察，無偏私。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he presided over the capital personnel evaluation and showed no partiality.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he presided over the capital personnel review and showed no favoritism.

sentences.zh: 嘗兼署戶、工二部事，綜理精密。

translations.literal: He once concurrently directed the affairs of the Ministries of Revenue and Works and managed them with meticulous precision.
translations.idiomatic: He also served concurrently in the Ministries of Revenue and Works, managing both with meticulous care.

sentences.zh: 奏行軫恤行戶四事，商困大蘇。

translations.literal: He memorialized and implemented four measures to relieve and show compassion to traveling merchant households, and merchant distress was greatly alleviated.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized four measures to relieve traveling merchant households, greatly easing their hardship.

sentences.zh: 外城陵垣，多所繕治，費皆取公帑奇羨，不以煩民。

translations.literal: The outer walls and mausoleum ramparts were extensively repaired; the costs were all taken from surplus public funds and did not burden the people.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw extensive repairs to the outer city walls and imperial mausoleum ramparts, funding the work entirely from surplus public funds without burdening the populace.

sentences.zh: 召為禮部右侍郎，四辭不允，越二年始受任。

translations.literal: He was summoned to be Right Vice Minister of Rites; he declined four times without acceptance, and only after two years did he take up the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as Right Vice Minister of Rites. He declined four times before the emperor would accept his refusal; only after two years did he take up the post.

sentences.zh: 時已進左侍郎，遂代郭正域視部事。

translations.literal: By then he had already been promoted to Left Vice Minister and thereupon replaced Guo Zhengyu in directing the ministry's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: By then he had already been promoted to Left Vice Minister and took over the ministry from Guo Zhengyu.

sentences.zh: 會楚王華奎因正域發其餽遺書，誣訐正域不法數事。

translations.literal: It happened that the Prince of Chu, Hua Kui, because Zhengyu exposed his gift-giving correspondence, falsely accused Zhengyu of several unlawful acts.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Zhengyu exposed correspondence revealing gifts from the Prince of Chu, Hua Kui, the prince retaliated with false accusations of misconduct.

sentences.zh: 廷機意右楚王，而微為正域解。

translations.literal: Tingji's intent favored the Prince of Chu, yet he subtly offered explanations on Zhengyu's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Tingji leaned toward the Prince of Chu, but quietly offered mitigating explanations for Zhengyu.

sentences.zh: 大學士沈一貫欲藉妖書傾正域，廷機與御史沈裕、同官塗宗浚俱署名上趨定生光獄，株連遂絕。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Shen Yiguan wished to use the demonic book case to bring down Zhengyu; Tingji, together with Censor Shen Yu and his colleague Tu Zongjun, all signed a memorial urging that the case of Li Shengguang be settled, and the chain of implicated persons was thereby cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Shen Yiguan sought to use the "demonic book" case to destroy Guo Zhengyu. Tingji, Censor Shen Yu, and his colleague Tu Zongjun all signed a memorial urging a swift verdict in the Li Shengguang case, cutting short the widening web of accusations.

sentences.zh: 三十三年夏，雷震郊壇。

translations.literal: In the summer of the thirty-third year, lightning struck the suburban altar.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the thirty-third year, lightning struck the suburban sacrificial altar.

sentences.zh: 既率同列條上修省事宜，復言今日闕失，莫如礦稅，宜罷撤。

translations.literal: Having already led his colleagues in itemizing and submitting matters for self-examination and reform, he again said that among today's failings none matched the mining tax and that it ought to be abolished and withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: He had already joined his colleagues in submitting a detailed program of self-reform; he now argued that of all the empire's current failings, none was graver than the mining tax, which ought to be abolished.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: There was no response.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not respond.

sentences.zh: 其冬，類上四方災異。

translations.literal: That winter he successively submitted reports on calamities and anomalies from the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he submitted successive reports on disasters and portents from across the empire.

sentences.zh: 秦王誼漶由中尉進封，其庶長子應授本爵，夤緣欲封郡王，廷機三疏力持。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin, Yi Huan, had been advanced in enfeoffment from Guard Commander; his eldest son by a concubine ought to have received the original title, but through backdoor influence sought enfeoffment as Commandery Prince; Tingji three times memorialized and firmly held his ground.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin, Yi Huan, had been promoted from Guard Commander to Commandery Prince; his eldest son by a concubine was entitled only to the original lower rank, but through influence sought promotion to Commandery Prince. Tingji submitted three memorials firmly opposing the request.

sentences.zh: 王遣人居間，廷機固拒，特旨許之。

translations.literal: The prince sent someone to intercede; Tingji firmly refused, but a special edict granted the request.
translations.idiomatic: The prince sent intermediaries to sway him, but Tingji stood firm—until an imperial special edict granted the request anyway.

sentences.zh: 益府服內請封，亦持不可。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yi's request for enfeoffment while still in mourning was also opposed as impermissible.
translations.idiomatic: He also blocked a request from the Prince of Yi's household for enfeoffment during the mourning period.

sentences.zh: 廷機遇事有執，尤廉潔，帝知之。

translations.literal: Tingji was firm in handling affairs and was especially incorrupt; the emperor knew this.
translations.idiomatic: Tingji was principled in office and notably incorruptible, and the emperor was aware of it.

sentences.zh: 然性刻深，亦頗偏愎，不諳大體。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was harsh and deep, and he was also rather obstinate and willful, not understanding the larger pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was harsh by nature, somewhat obstinate, and lacked a grasp of the larger picture.

sentences.zh: 楚宗人華勣以奏訐楚王，撫按官既擬奪爵，錮高墻，廷機授《祖訓》謀害親王例，議置之死。

translations.literal: A clansman of Chu, Hua Xu, because he memorialized and denounced the Prince of Chu, after the provincial and surveillance officials had already proposed stripping his title and imprisoning him behind the high wall, Tingji applied the precedent in the Ancestral Instructions for plotting harm against an imperial prince and proposed putting him to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Hua Xu, a member of the Chu imperial clan, denounced the Prince of Chu in a memorial, the provincial officials had already proposed stripping his title and imprisoning him. Tingji invoked the Ancestral Instructions' precedent for plotting against an imperial prince and argued for the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 言路勢張，政府暨銓曹畏之，不敢出諸外，年例遂廢。

translations.literal: The remonstrating officials were powerful; the chief ministers and the Ministry of Personnel feared them and dared not release the case publicly, and the annual precedent was thus abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The censorial officials were at the height of their power; the chief ministers and the Ministry of Personnel feared them and dared not make the case public, and the annual review precedent was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 禮部主事聶雲翰論之，廷機希言路意，中雲翰察典。

translations.literal: Principal Secretary of Rites Nie Yunhan criticized this; Tingji, seeking to align with the remonstrators' intent, struck Yunhan in the annual evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: Nie Yunhan, a principal secretary in the Ministry of Rites, criticized the decision. Seeking to placate the censorial faction, Tingji marked Yunhan down in the annual performance review.

sentences.zh: 給事中袁懋謙劾之。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Yuan Maoqian impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Yuan Maoqian impeached him.

sentences.zh: 廷機求退，不允。

translations.literal: Tingji requested to retire; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Tingji asked to resign, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 時內閣止朱賡一人。

translations.literal: At the time the Grand Secretariat had only Zhu Geng alone.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhu Geng was the sole member of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 給事中王元翰等慮廷機且入輔，數陰詆之。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretaries Wang Yuanhan and others, fearing that Tingji would soon enter as an assistant minister, repeatedly slandered him in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretaries Wang Yuanhan and others, fearing that Tingji would soon join the Grand Secretariat, repeatedly attacked him behind the scenes.

sentences.zh: 三十五年夏，廷推閣臣，廷機果與焉。

translations.literal: In the summer of the thirty-fifth year, when Grand Secretaries were court-recommended, Tingji was indeed among them.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the thirty-fifth year, when the court recommended candidates for the Grand Secretariat, Tingji was among them.

sentences.zh: 給事中曹於忭、宋一韓、御史陳宗契不可。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretaries Cao Yubin and Song Yihan and Censor Chen Zongqi objected.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretaries Cao Yubin and Song Yihan and Censor Chen Zongqi objected.

sentences.zh: 相持久之，卒列以上。

translations.literal: The standoff was prolonged, but in the end he was listed at the top.
translations.idiomatic: The dispute dragged on, but in the end Tingji was ranked first.

sentences.zh: 帝雅重廷機，命以禮部尚書兼東閣大學士，入參機務。

translations.literal: The emperor had long valued Tingji and ordered him to serve as Minister of Rites and concurrent Eastern Pavilion Grand Secretary, entering to take part in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long held Tingji in high regard and appointed him Minister of Rites and Eastern Pavilion Grand Secretary, entrusting him with affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 廷機三辭始視事。

translations.literal: Tingji declined three times before he took up his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Tingji declined three times before finally assuming his duties.

sentences.zh: 元翰及給事中胡忻攻之不已，帝為奪俸，以慰廷機。

translations.literal: Yuanhan and Supervising Secretary Hu Xin attacked him without cease; the emperor stripped their salaries on his behalf to console Tingji.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhan and Supervising Secretary Hu Xin kept up their attacks; the emperor suspended their salaries to reassure Tingji.

sentences.zh: 已而姜士昌、宋燾復以論廷機被黜，群情益憤。

translations.literal: Before long, Jiang Shichang and Song Tao were again dismissed for having criticized Tingji, and public sentiment grew all the more indignant.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, Jiang Shichang and Song Tao were dismissed yet again for speaking out against Tingji, and outrage in the ranks only deepened.

sentences.zh: 廷機力辨求罷，又疏陳十宜去，帝慰諭有加。

translations.literal: Tingji argued vigorously and sought dismissal; he also memorialized setting forth ten reasons he ought to leave. The emperor comforted and instructed him with added favor.
translations.idiomatic: Tingji pleaded his case forcefully and asked to be relieved, memorializing ten reasons he ought to resign; the emperor replied with warm reassurance and still greater favor.

sentences.zh: 明年四月，主事鄭振先論賡十二罪，並及廷機。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the following year, Section Chief Zheng Zhenxian memorialized twelve crimes of Geng and also implicated Tingji.
translations.idiomatic: The next April, Section Chief Zheng Zhenxian submitted a memorial listing twelve crimes of Zhu Geng and implicating Tingji as well.

sentences.zh: 廷機累疏乞休，杜門數月不出。

translations.literal: Tingji repeatedly memorialized begging to retire and shut his gates, not going out for many months.
translations.idiomatic: Tingji sent memorial after memorial begging leave of office and shut himself indoors, refusing to emerge for months on end.

sentences.zh: 言者疑其偽，數十人交章力攻。

translations.literal: Memorialists suspected it was feigned, and several dozen submitted memorials in succession attacking him with force.
translations.idiomatic: Critics suspected he was feigning illness, and dozens of officials submitted memorial after memorial demanding his removal.

sentences.zh: 廷機求去不已，帝屢詔勉留，且遣鴻臚趣出，堅臥不起。

translations.literal: Tingji's pleas to leave did not cease. The emperor repeatedly issued edicts urging him to stay, and even sent the Director of Ceremonies to hasten him out; he lay firm and would not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Tingji kept pressing to resign. The emperor repeatedly issued edicts urging him to stay, even dispatching the Director of Ceremonies to summon him forth—but he stayed in bed and would not budge.

sentences.zh: 待命逾年，乃屏居荒廟，廷臣猶有繁言。

translations.literal: Awaiting orders for more than a year, he then withdrew to live sequestered in a desolate temple; court ministers still had much to say.
translations.idiomatic: After waiting more than a year for a decision, he withdrew to live in a ruined temple; court officials still had plenty to say about him.

sentences.zh: 至四十年九月，疏已百二十餘上，乃陛辭出都待命。

translations.literal: By the ninth month of the fortieth year, he had submitted more than one hundred and twenty memorials, then took leave at court and went out of the capital to await orders.
translations.idiomatic: By the ninth month of the fortieth year, having submitted more than a hundred and twenty memorials, he formally took leave of the emperor and left the capital to await final orders.

sentences.zh: 同官葉向高言廷機已行，不可再挽，乃加太子太保。

translations.literal: His colleague Ye Xianggao said Tingji had already departed and could not be held back again; he was then promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His colleague Ye Xianggao argued that Tingji was already on his way and could not be recalled; the court then added to his titles the post of Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 賜道里費，乘傳，以行人護歸。

translations.literal: He was granted traveling expenses, rode the relay post, and was escorted home by a courier official.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted travel expenses, given use of the imperial courier service, and sent home under the escort of a palace messenger.

sentences.zh: 居四年卒。

translations.literal: After four years at home, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later he died.

sentences.zh: 贈少保，謚文節。

translations.literal: He was posthumously promoted to Junior Guardian and given the posthumous name Wenzijie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Junior Guardian and given the posthumous title Wenjie.

sentences.zh: 廷機系閣籍六年，秉政止九月，無大過。

translations.literal: Tingji was on the Grand Secretariat roster for six years and held power for only nine months, with no major fault.
translations.idiomatic: Tingji had been enrolled on the Grand Secretariat roster for six years and actually held power for only nine months, with no major misdeeds to his name.

sentences.zh: 言路以其與申時行、沈一貫輩密相授受，故交章逐之。

translations.literal: The remonstrance officials, because he had secretly exchanged favors with Shen Shixing, Shen Yiguan, and their like, therefore submitted successive memorials to drive him out.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial officials attacked him in waves because they believed he had been in secret league with Shen Shixing, Shen Yiguan, and their faction.

sentences.zh: 輔臣以齮龁受辱，屏棄積年而後去，前此未有也。

translations.literal: For an assisting minister to suffer insult through petty grudges, be cast aside for accumulated years, and only then leave — there had never been such a case before.
translations.idiomatic: That a grand secretary should be hounded by petty slander, cast aside for years, and driven out only after a long ordeal was without precedent.

sentences.zh: 廷機輔政時，四川巡撫喬璧星銳欲討鎮雄安堯臣，與貴州守臣持議不決。

translations.literal: When Tingji assisted in governing, Sichuan Grand Coordinator Qiao Bixing was eager to campaign against An Yaochén, commander of Zhen'an, but he and the Guizhou defending officials could not settle their debate.
translations.idiomatic: While Tingji was in office, Sichuan Grand Coordinator Qiao Bixing was eager to launch a punitive campaign against An Yaochén, military commander of Zhen'an, but he and the Guizhou provincial officials deadlocked over the decision.

sentences.zh: 廷機力主撤兵，其後卒無事，議者稱之。

translations.literal: Tingji vigorously advocated withdrawing the troops; afterward in the end nothing happened, and commentators praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Tingji strongly argued for withdrawing the troops; in the event nothing came of the affair, and later commentators praised his judgment.

sentences.zh: 閩人入閣，自楊榮、陳山後，以語言難曉，垂二百年無人，廷機始與葉向高並命。

translations.literal: For a Fujian native to enter the Grand Secretariat, after Yang Rong and Chen Shan, because the speech was hard to understand, for nearly two hundred years there had been none; Tingji was the first to be appointed together with Ye Xianggao.
translations.idiomatic: No native of Fujian had entered the Grand Secretariat since Yang Rong and Chen Shan—nearly two centuries earlier—because their accents were hard for others to follow; Tingji was the first to break that drought, appointed alongside Ye Xianggao.

sentences.zh: 後周如磐、張瑞圖、林釬、蔣德璘、黃景昉復相繼云。

translations.literal: Later Zhou Rupan, Zhang Ruitu, Lin Qian, Jiang Delin, and Huang Jingfang followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou Rupan, Zhang Ruitu, Lin Qian, Jiang Delin, and Huang Jingfang would follow in succession.

sentences.zh: 吳道南

translations.literal: Wu Daonan
translations.idiomatic: Wu Daonan

sentences.zh: 吳道南，字會甫，崇仁人。

translations.literal: Wu Daonan, style name Huifu, was a native of Chongren.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Daonan, whose style name was Huifu, came from Chongren.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十七年進士及第。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Wanli he graduated as a presented scholar at the palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of the Wanli reign he passed the palace examination and received his jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 授編修，進左中允。

translations.literal: He was appointed Compiler, then promoted to Left Righteousness Master.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a Hanlin Compiler and later promoted to Left Sub-Reader of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 直講東宮，太子偶旁矚，道南即輟講拱俟，太子為改容。

translations.literal: He lectured directly in the Eastern Palace. When the crown prince chanced to glance aside, Daonan at once stopped lecturing and stood with hands clasped awaiting him; the crown prince changed his bearing.
translations.idiomatic: While lecturing in the Eastern Palace, he once noticed the crown prince glance away; Daonan immediately stopped speaking and stood with hands clasped, waiting; the prince straightened up at once.

sentences.zh: 歷左諭德少詹事。

translations.literal: He served successively as Left Preceptor and Junior Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of Left Preceptor and Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 擢禮部右侍郎，署部事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Rites and administered the ministry's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites and put in charge of the ministry's business.

sentences.zh: 歷城、高苑牛產犢，皆兩首兩鼻，道南請盡蠲山東諸稅，召還內臣，又因災異言貂珰斂怨，乞下詔罪己，與天下更新。

translations.literal: In Licheng and Gaoyuan, oxen bore calves, all with two heads and two noses. Daonan requested that all taxes in Shandong be entirely remitted, that eunuchs be recalled, and furthermore citing calamities and portents, said that sable-clad palace attendants were gathering resentments; he begged that the emperor issue an edict blaming himself and renew the realm together with all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In Licheng and Gaoyuan oxen bore deformed calves, each with two heads and two noses. Daonan memorialized to remit all Shandong levies, recall inner-court eunuchs from the provinces, and—citing strange omens—warn that palace commissioners were stoking popular resentment; he urged the emperor to issue a self-reproach edict and inaugurate a fresh start for the realm.

sentences.zh: 皆不報。

translations.literal: None received reply.
translations.idiomatic: None of his proposals received a response.

sentences.zh: 尋請追諡文朝忠臣。

translations.literal: Soon he requested posthumous honors for loyal officials of the Jianwen reign.
translations.idiomatic: He soon memorialized to grant posthumous titles to the loyal officials of the Jianwen reign.

sentences.zh: 京師久旱，疏言：「天下人情鬱而不散，致成旱災。

translations.literal: The capital had long been dry; in a memorial he said: "The feelings of people throughout the realm are pent up and do not disperse, causing drought calamity.
translations.idiomatic: After a prolonged drought in the capital, he memorialized: "The grievances of the people throughout the realm are pent up and cannot disperse, and this has brought on drought.

sentences.zh: 如東宮天下本，不使講明經術，練習政務，久置深闈，聰明隔塞，鬱一也。

translations.literal: For example, the Eastern Palace is the root of the realm; yet one does not have it expound the classics and study statecraft, but keeps it long in the inner quarters. Its brilliance is blocked and sealed — this is the first grievance.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace is the foundation of the realm, yet the heir is not taught the classics or trained in affairs of state, but kept long in the inner quarters with his talents stifled — that is the first grievance.

sentences.zh: 法司懸缺半載，讞鞫無人，囹圄充滿，有入無出，愁憤之氣，上薄日星，鬱二也。

translations.literal: The judicial offices have had vacancies for half a year; there is no one to try cases. Prisons are filled to overflowing; people enter but do not leave. The air of grief and rage rises to touch the sun and stars — this is the second grievance.
translations.idiomatic: The judicial offices have stood vacant for half a year with no one to hear cases; the prisons are packed full, with prisoners entering but never leaving. Grief and rage rise to heaven itself — that is the second grievance.

sentences.zh: 內藏山積，而閭閻半菽不充，曾不發帑振救，坐視其死亡轉徙，鬱三也。

translations.literal: The inner treasury is piled mountain-high, yet in the lanes and alleys half cannot fill their bellies with beans; the authorities never opened the coffers to relieve disaster, but sat and watched death and displacement — this is the third grievance.
translations.idiomatic: The inner treasury is piled high, yet in the lanes and alleys people can scarcely fill half a bowl with beans; the court never opens the coffers for relief but sits by while people die or flee — that is the third grievance.

sentences.zh: 累臣滿朝薦、卞孔時，時稱循吏，因權珰構陷，一系數年，鬱四也。

translations.literal: Imprisoned officials fill the court — Man Chaojian and Bian Kongshi, at the time called upright administrators, were framed by powerful eunuchs and imprisoned for several years — this is the fourth grievance.
translations.idiomatic: Imprisoned officials crowd the court — Man Chaojian and Bian Kongshi, once praised as model magistrates, were framed by powerful eunuchs and held for years — that is the fourth grievance.

sentences.zh: 廢棄諸臣，實堪世用，一斥不復，山林終老，鬱五也。

translations.literal: Dismissed officials who were truly fit for public service are cast out once and never restored, to end their days in the mountains and forests — this is the fifth grievance.
translations.idiomatic: Capable officials cast aside are dismissed once and never recalled, to end their days in obscurity — that is the fifth grievance.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠渙發德音，除此數鬱，不崇朝而雨露遍天下矣。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty will truly issue benevolent words and remove these several grievances, within a single morning dew and rain will spread across the realm."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will truly issue words of grace and lift these burdens, relief will spread across the realm before the morning is out."

sentences.zh: 帝不省。

translations.literal: The emperor did not heed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took no notice.

sentences.zh: 道南遇事有操執，明達政體。

translations.literal: Daonan in handling affairs had firm principle and understood the body of government.
translations.idiomatic: In office Daonan acted with firm principle and a clear grasp of government.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮貢使歸，請市火藥，執不予。

translations.literal: A Korean tribute envoy on returning requested to purchase gunpowder; he firmly refused to grant it.
translations.idiomatic: When a Korean tribute envoy requested gunpowder for purchase on his return journey, he refused.

sentences.zh: 土魯番貢玉，請勿納。

translations.literal: Turfan presented jade in tribute; he requested that it not be accepted.
translations.idiomatic: When Turfan offered jade as tribute, he argued against accepting it.

sentences.zh: 遼東議開科試士，以巖疆當重武，格不行。

translations.literal: Liaodong proposed opening examinations to test scholars; on the grounds that a strategic frontier should emphasize military affairs, he blocked it from proceeding.
translations.idiomatic: When Liaodong proposed holding civil examinations, he vetoed the plan on the grounds that a strategic frontier must prioritize military strength.

sentences.zh: 父喪歸。

translations.literal: On his father's death he returned home in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 服闋，即家拜禮部尚書兼東閣大學士，預機務，與方從哲並命。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was appointed from home as Minister of Rites and concurrent Eastern Pavilion Grand Secretary, to take part in state affairs, appointed together with Fang Congzhe.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning period ended, he was appointed from home as Minister of Rites and Eastern Pavilion Grand Secretary, charged with affairs of state alongside Fang Congzhe.

sentences.zh: 三辭不允，久之始入朝。

translations.literal: He declined three times without assent; only after a long time did he enter court.
translations.idiomatic: He declined three times before accepting; only after a long delay did he come to court.

sentences.zh: 故事，廷臣受官，先面謝乃蒞任。

translations.literal: By precedent, when court ministers received office they first took leave to give thanks in audience before assuming their post.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, newly appointed ministers were to appear before the emperor to give thanks before taking up their duties.

sentences.zh: 帝不視朝久，皆先蒞任。

translations.literal: The emperor had not held court for a long time, and all assumed their posts first.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long absent himself from court, so everyone simply assumed their posts without an audience.

sentences.zh: 道南至，不獲見，不敢入直。

translations.literal: When Daonan arrived he could not obtain an audience and dared not enter duty.
translations.idiomatic: When Daonan arrived he could not obtain an audience and refused to take up his duties in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 同官從哲為言，帝令先視事，道南疏謝。

translations.literal: His colleague Congzhe spoke on his behalf; the emperor ordered him first to oversee affairs; Daonan memorialized thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Congzhe interceded for him; the emperor told him to assume his duties first; Daonan submitted a memorial of thanks.

sentences.zh: 居數日，言：「臣就列經旬，僅下瑞王婚禮一疏。

translations.literal: After several days he said: "Your servant has taken my place for more than ten days, and only one memorial on the Rui Prince's wedding ceremony has gone forth.
translations.idiomatic: After several days he memorialized: "Your servant has taken up my post for more than ten days, yet only one memorial on the Rui Prince's wedding has been issued.

sentences.zh: 他若儲宮出講、諸王豫教、簡大僚、舉遺失、撤稅使、補言官諸事，廷臣舌敝以請者，舉皆杳然，豈陛下簡置臣等意。」

translations.literal: Other matters such as the crown prince coming forth to lecture, princes receiving preliminary instruction, selecting great officials, recommending the overlooked, withdrawing tax commissioners, and filling remonstrance posts — for all of which court ministers have worn out their tongues in petition — there has been no response at all. Is this truly Your Majesty's intention in selecting and appointing us?"
translations.idiomatic: As for the crown prince's education, princely instruction, appointing senior officials, recommending overlooked talent, withdrawing tax commissioners, and filling remonstrance posts — matters on which court ministers have pleaded until their tongues are worn — there has been no response at all. Is this truly what Your Majesty intended when you appointed us?"

sentences.zh: 帝優詔答之，卒不行。

translations.literal: The emperor replied with a gracious edict, but in the end nothing was carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied with a gracious edict, but in the end acted on none of it.

sentences.zh: 迨帝因「梃擊」之變，召見群臣慈寧宮。

translations.literal: Only when the emperor, because of the "Staff Assault" affair, summoned the ministers to audience at Cining Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the emperor summoned the court to Cining Palace in the wake of the "Staff Assault" incident did he receive them.

sentences.zh: 道南始得面謝，自是不獲再見。

translations.literal: Daonan only then obtained leave to give thanks in audience; from then on he never obtained another audience.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Daonan get his long-awaited audience; he never saw the emperor again.

sentences.zh: 織造中官劉成死，遣其黨呂貴往護，貴嗾奸民留己督造。

translations.literal: The eunuch Liu Cheng of the Weaving Directorate died; his faction member Lü Gui was sent to oversee the funeral, and Gui incited scoundrels to have himself kept on to supervise manufacture.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Cheng, the eunuch overseer of the Weaving Directorate, died, his ally Lü Gui was dispatched to handle affairs; Gui schemed with local ruffians to have himself retained as supervisor of production.

sentences.zh: 中旨許之，命草敕。

translations.literal: A secret edict approved it and ordered a patent of appointment drafted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the request by secret edict and ordered a patent of appointment drafted.

sentences.zh: 道南偕從哲爭，且詢疏所從進，請永杜內降，弗聽。

translations.literal: Daonan together with Congzhe objected, and moreover inquired from what channel the memorial had entered; he requested that inner edicts be permanently blocked — this was not heard.
translations.idiomatic: Daonan and Fang Congzhe protested and demanded to know who had forwarded the request; they asked that secret edicts from the inner palace be abolished once and for all—but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽故無商稅，中官為稅使，置關湖口征課。

translations.literal: Poyang had never had merchant taxes; a eunuch served as tax commissioner and established a checkpoint at Hukou to levy duties.
translations.idiomatic: Poyang had never levied merchant taxes, but a eunuch tax commissioner established a checkpoint at Hukou to collect duties.

sentences.zh: 道南極言傍湖舟無所泊，多覆沒，請罷關勿征，亦不納。

translations.literal: Daonan spoke at extreme length that boats along the lake had nowhere to moor and many were capsized; he requested that the checkpoint be abolished and duties not levied — this too was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Daonan argued forcefully that boats on the lake had nowhere to moor and many were sinking; he pleaded to close the checkpoint and end the levies—but that too was rejected.

sentences.zh: 道南輔大政不為詭隨，頗有時望。

translations.literal: Daonan in assisting great affairs was not accommodating and slippery; he had considerable standing in his time.
translations.idiomatic: As a grand secretary Daonan refused to bend with every wind and enjoyed considerable repute at court.

sentences.zh: 歲丙辰，偕禮部尚書劉楚先典會試。

translations.literal: In the year bingchen he together with Minister of Rites Liu Chuxian presided over the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the bingchen year he and Minister of Rites Liu Chuxian served as chief examiners of the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 吳江舉人沈同和者，副都御史季文子，目不知書，賄禮部吏，與同里趙鳴陽聯號舍。

translations.literal: A Wu County candidate Shen Tonghe was the son of Vice Censor-in-Chief Ji Wen; his eyes did not know books. He bribed a Ministry of Rites clerk and shared an examination cell with his fellow townsman Zhao Mingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Tonghe of Wu County, son of Vice Censor-in-Chief Shen Jiwen, was illiterate; he bribed a Ministry of Rites clerk and was assigned an examination cell alongside his neighbor Zhao Mingyang.

sentences.zh: 其首場七篇，自坊刻外，皆鳴陽筆也。

translations.literal: Of his seven essays for the first session, apart from those from commercial editions, all were in Mingyang's hand.
translations.idiomatic: Of the seven essays he submitted for the first session, all but those copied from commercial editions were written by Zhao Mingyang.

sentences.zh: 榜發，同和第一，鳴陽亦中式，都下大嘩。

translations.literal: When the list was issued, Tonghe was first and Mingyang also passed; the capital was in great uproar.
translations.idiomatic: When the results were posted, Tonghe ranked first and Mingyang also passed—provoking an uproar throughout the capital.

sentences.zh: 道南等亟檢舉，詔令覆試。

translations.literal: Daonan and others swiftly reported the case; an edict ordered a re-examination.
translations.idiomatic: Daonan and his colleagues immediately reported the fraud; the emperor ordered a re-examination.

sentences.zh: 同和竟日構一文。

translations.literal: Tonghe spent the whole day composing one essay.
translations.idiomatic: Tonghe managed to compose a single essay only after an entire day's struggle.

sentences.zh: 下吏，戍煙瘴，鳴陽亦除名。

translations.literal: He was handed over to officials, sent to exile in the miasmic south; Mingyang was also struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Tonghe was handed over to the authorities and exiled to the malarial south; Mingyang was struck from the rolls as well.

sentences.zh: 先是，湯賓尹科場事，實道南發之，其黨側目。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the examination hall affair of Tang Binyin, it was in fact Daonan who had exposed it; his faction looked askance.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, it was Daonan who had exposed the examination fraud involving Tang Binyin; his enemies watched him with hostile eyes.

sentences.zh: 御史李嵩、周師旦遂連章論道南，而給事中劉文炳攻尤力。

translations.literal: Censors Li Song and Zhou Shidan then submitted successive memorials attacking Daonan, while Supervising Secretary Liu Wenbing attacked with especial force.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Li Song and Zhou Shidan followed with memorial after memorial denouncing Daonan, and Supervising Secretary Liu Wenbing led the attack.

sentences.zh: 道南疏辨乞休，頗侵文炳。

translations.literal: Daonan memorialized in self-defense begging to retire, and rather infringed upon Wenbing.
translations.idiomatic: Daonan replied in a memorial defending himself and asking to resign, sharply rebuking Liu Wenbing in the process.

sentences.zh: 文炳遂極詆御史張至發助之。

translations.literal: Wenbing then slandered to the extreme Censor Zhang Zhifa, who assisted him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing then launched a blistering attack, joined by Censor Zhang Zhifa.

sentences.zh: 道南不能堪，言：「臺諫劾閣臣，職也，未有肆口嫚罵者。

translations.literal: Daonan could not bear it and said: "For censorial and remonstrance officials to impeach Grand Secretaries is their duty; yet there has never been one who opened his mouth in wanton reviling.
translations.idiomatic: Daonan could bear it no longer and memorialized: "For censorial and remonstrance officials to impeach grand secretaries is their duty—but never before has one descended to open abuse.

sentences.zh: 臣辱國已甚，請立罷黜。」

translations.literal: Your servant has shamed the state too greatly; I beg to be dismissed at once."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has shamed the state beyond measure; I beg to be dismissed at once."

sentences.zh: 帝雅重道南，謫文炳外任，奪嵩等俸。

translations.literal: The emperor had long valued Daonan; he demoted Wenbing to an outer post and stripped Song and the others of salaries.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, who had long valued Daonan, demoted Wenbing to a provincial post and suspended the salaries of Li Song and the others.

sentences.zh: 御史韓浚、朱堦救文炳，復詆道南。

translations.literal: Censors Han Jun and Zhu Jie came to Wenbing's defense and again slandered Daonan.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Han Jun and Zhu Jie rallied to Wenbing's defense and renewed their attacks on Daonan.

sentences.zh: 道南益求去。

translations.literal: Daonan all the more sought to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Daonan pressed harder to resign.

sentences.zh: 杜門逾年，疏二十七上，帝猶勉留。

translations.literal: He shut his gates for more than a year; twenty-seven memorials went up; the emperor still urged him to stay.
translations.idiomatic: He shut himself indoors for more than a year, submitting twenty-seven memorials begging leave; the emperor still urged him to remain.

sentences.zh: 會繼母訃至，乃賜道里費，遣行人護歸。

translations.literal: When news arrived of his stepmother's death, he was then granted traveling expenses and a palace messenger was sent to escort him home.
translations.idiomatic: When word came of his stepmother's death, the court granted him travel expenses and dispatched a palace messenger to escort him home.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，以覃恩即家進太子太保。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign, by a grace amnesty he was promoted from home to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianqi reign he was promoted at home to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent as part of a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 居二年卒。

translations.literal: After two years at home he died.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he died.

sentences.zh: 贈少保，謚文恪。

translations.literal: He was posthumously promoted to Junior Guardian and given the posthumous name Wenke.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Junior Guardian and given the posthumous title Wenkew.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：《傳》稱「道合則服從，不合則去」，其王家屏、沈鯉之謂乎！

translations.literal: The eulogist says: The "Record" says, "When the Way accorded, then serve and follow; when it did not accord, then leave" — is this not what is meant of Wang Jiabing and Shen Li!
translations.idiomatic: The eulogist writes: The Record says, "When the Way aligns, serve; when it does not, depart"—surely this describes Wang Jiabing and Shen Li!

sentences.zh: 廷機雖頗叢物議，然清節不汙。

translations.literal: Tingji, although he drew much public criticism, yet his pure integrity was not stained.
translations.idiomatic: Though Tingji drew considerable controversy, his integrity remained unstained.

sentences.zh: 若于陛之世德，慎行之博聞，亦足稱羽儀廊廟之選矣。

translations.literal: As for Yubi's inherited virtue and Shenxing's broad learning, they too suffice to be called selections of feathered adornment for the court and temple.
translations.idiomatic: As for Chen Yubi's inherited virtue and Yu Shenxing's erudition, they too were worthy ornaments of the imperial council.
